title: Agent OS file tree

source.repo: the files in git (without the old planning folder), their folders and the local keys files, with every item's metadata files

sync: Built by the ide-build scripts from the files on disk and the metadata files next to each item. The page saves straight away into its own store (collections inputs, nodes, changes); at a sync ("sync the file tree") the project IDE agent saves them word for word, writes edits into their files and rebuilds this file.

status_legend.proposed: an agent's proposal, waiting for the owner
status_legend.placeholder: a pattern such as [agent-name]; real names come later

decisions.text: Keep symlinks for shared things: Shared things (configs, workers, sub-agents, scripts, logs, data) stay in shared places and reach an agent's folder through symlinks, not copies. This settles the v0.1 idea "needed files are symlinked into the agent's folder".
Every symlink has .link in its name: Every symlinked file or folder has `.link` in its name, so a link can be told from a real file by its name alone.
Per-agent docs live centrally: Each agent's docs lived in `docs/agents/[domain]/[agent-name]/` and were linked into the agent folder as `docs.link/`.

One docs root with common knowledge, indexes, schemas, flows and metrics: `docs/` is the single docs root. Besides the vision it holds common knowledge (`common/`), an index of all things (`index/`), `data-schemas.md`, `flows.md` and `metrics.md`.
Data as JSON and Markdown files for now: All data, configs and logs are plain JSON, JSONL and Markdown files for now. No database.

Two config types: global and per agent: Configs come in two types for now: one global `system.config.json` with sections (split into files later when a section gets long) and one config per agent. Which settings are common and which are individual is worked out with example agents.

Workers are scripts: Workers are just scripts. All scripts live in `scripts/`: workers, decision (buy/sell) and system scripts, either shared or per agent. Workers are described in config: which exist, their schedule, how they run, what they are for.
Sub-agents are Claude Code sub-agents: Sub-agents are Claude Code sub-agents under `.claude/agents/`, not a separate `subagents/` folder. For now only system-wide ones exist.
Logs are organised by source: Shared logs are organised by source (system, services, workers, sub-agents), and some are linked into agents.
Data is organised by source: Shared data is organised by source (system, workers, sub-agents), and some is linked into agents.
Model and platform routing is config: Which platform and model each agent, sub-agent and AI worker uses is config in its own file, `models.config.json`. There is no `platforms-and-models/` folder.

Every agent has a globally unique name: Every agent's name is unique across all domains and is its ID everywhere: folder, configs, logs, data, docs, indexes, UI and routes. The agents index is the registry and create-agent checks it.
System is a domain: `system` is a domain like the trading domains. Domains sit directly under `agents/` (`agents/system/`, `agents/prediction-market-agents/`, `agents/copy-trading-agents/`).

Every agent has the same folders with its own real files: Every agent, system and trading alike, has the same folders `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, holding its own real files. At the time each also had a `system.link/` folder link to the system folder of the same kind.

The system holds the shared files and sees every agent: The system domain has the same folders, holding the shared files, plus `agents/[agent-name].link/` views of every agent's folder of the same kind, giving one view over everything.
.claude/ at every domain and strategy level: `.claude/` exists at every domain level (including system) and at every strategy level. At the time, each agent's own `.claude/` linked them in.

Docs follow the same pattern: Docs follow the same pattern as configs, scripts, logs and data. Each agent has a real `docs/` (README, strategy, changes, decisions, notes). The shared docs move from the top-level `docs/` to `agents/system/docs/`. The repo root keeps only `README.md`, which points there.

Domain owner and self-improvement are sub-agents: There are no separate folders for domain agents or self-improvement agents. The domain owner is a sub-agent in the domain's `.claude/agents/`. Self-improvement is a sub-agent at every `.claude/` level, scoped to that level. Their memory was proposed in `agents/system/data/subagents/[name]/`.

.claude links go parent to child only: `.claude` links go from parent to child only (system, then domains, then strategies, then agents); lower levels never link up. We also proposed that every run starts at the top, which D-021 withdrew.

Agents link individual files: Inside an agent's `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/` and `docs/` there are no folder links. There are individual file links (`[name].link.[ext]`), only to the files that agent's logic needs, from any folder. The set is chosen at creation and updated by self-improvement.

No domain links to strategies' agents and skills: The domain level has no `.claude` links down to its strategies' sub-agents and skills. Our proposal in its place: each level runs in its own folder, a trading agent runs in its own folder, and higher-level sub-agents hand their results to agents as data files linked per D-020.

Three agent levels, one identical folder: There are three levels of agents, the system (manages all domains and system development), each domain and each strategy, and every agent folder has the identical file structure. Trading variants under a strategy have the same structure. The domain's own `CLAUDE.md` is the domain owner.

A secrets store outside agents/: Secrets live in a git-ignored `.secrets/` at the repo root, outside `agents/`, with `test/` and `live/` kept apart and a metadata index without values. Scripts load keys at run time through `load-secret`; secrets are never linked into agent folders, never logged and never put in LLM context. The owner asked for the store; the design was ours.

The standard .claude/ layout at every level: Every `.claude/` folder (system, domain, strategy, variant) follows the standard Claude Code layout, with `CLAUDE.md` inside `.claude/` rather than at the folder root. Only generic placeholders for now; concrete skills and logic come later.

Tests and research at every level: Every level has `tests/` with `agents/` (the prompt and sub-agents) and `scripts/` (code), each with a `tests.config.json` the owner can switch tests on and off in, run by one shared `run-tests` script that writes results back. Every level also has `research/` with an `index.json` history and one folder per item. Placement at the folder root and the fields are our proposal.

System-support roles are sub-agents: System-support roles (docs, development, improvement, analysis, research) are sub-agents in `agents/system/.claude/agents/`, not agent folders. A role that ever needs its own files and runs becomes a normal agent with the standard folder.

All test keys in one .env: All test keys live in one `.secrets/test/.env`, grouped in sections with prefixed names, and agents may read and update it. `live/.env` mirrors the same key names with live values, owner only, in a later phase. Scripts get only the keys their config declares, through the shared loader.

.gitignore is a real, commented file: The repo `.gitignore` is a real file in which every entry has a comment saying why: secrets, local Claude Code settings and memory, build junk. On 2026-09-30 the owner added runtime logs and data (content ignored, folders kept) and local Cursor state.

A jobs file for every agent: Every agent (system, domain, strategy, variant) has its own jobs file `configs/[name].workers.json`, where it can see, change and turn off everything it runs. A job is a script or an AI run (the agent, a sub-agent, skill, workflow or command) with a schedule, where it runs, the platform and the model. One central scheduler runs them all. The format is our proposal.

One content-folder template with subagents.link/: At every level, each content folder (`configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/`) holds the level's own files plus `subagents.link/` with one folder link per direct child agent, pointing at the child's folder of the same kind. Trading agents have no children, so no `subagents.link/`. For now no `.claude` folder is linked at any level.

A links file for every agent, and relink: Every agent layer has its own links file `configs/[name].links.json` saying what is linked from where: the system, its own domain or strategy, another domain, or any other agent by its unique name. One shared `relink` script builds every link from these files plus the child links, removes links nobody lists and checks them. It runs when a links file changes, at review time, and when an agent edits its own links file. The format and the triggers are our proposal.

Variant names start with their strategy: A variant's name starts with its strategy: `[strategy-id].[own-name]-v[N].[platform-model]-[test|live]`, e.g. `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test`. The strategy agent's ID also carries its main platform/model and its mode, e.g. `pm-strategy-1-agent.opus55-test`. The strategy agent, through its SI sub-agent [21.1.1.1], creates modifications of itself as new test variants, compares them and folds a winning change back into the strategy. The rule is the owner's; the exact format is our proposal.

One knowledge agent keeps a layered knowledge base: Every owner input (project chat, a thread, the File Tree page), every answer Claude gives to the owner's questions, and every change to the system goes through one knowledge agent, `sys-knowledge-agent` [10.1.1.2] (was `sys-docs-agent`). With its skills `knowledge-intake` [10.1.2.1] and `knowledge-summarise` [10.1.2.2] it stores the input word for word, puts each piece of knowledge in the one doc that owns it, updates everything that states the same thing, records decisions and history, and refreshes the "How it works" summary of every file and folder, bottom up. A knowledge map [2.18.8] links each doc section to the files and folders it applies to (many to many). Each summary can carry "Always keep in mind" lines. Decisions, concepts and rules are no longer separate lists on the page: their content lives in the topic docs, and this file is history.

Docs for people live in .claude/docs, one skill per doc: The docs are for people: plain, book-like, readable by a non-technical person, with no reference numbers, ids or decision codes; relations, decisions and sources are kept only in the agent's own notes (in-20261001-0800). Layout set by the owner: `.claude/agents/knowledge-base-agent.md` (the knowledge agent, renamed from `sys-knowledge-agent`), `.claude/docs/` with README.md (everything we know, regenerated after every update), file-tree.md, vision.md, architecture.md, glossary.md and more, plus subagents links to the children's docs; one skill per doc, starting with vision. Order: agent and vision skill for the owner to check, then vision.md, then the other docs one by one, file tree and mapping last; every round improves the agent and the skills. Every level has the same docs with its own specifics.

Answers on the vision: runs, approvals, first strategy, scope of actions: (1) At the end of every run an agent compresses or summarises what matters and clears what it no longer needs; it decides itself whether to keep or renew its session and whether to subscribe to more data, research or ask for a worker. (2) Runs also fire on agent-set triggers, e.g. when research it started is finished; that run gets all subscribed data plus the research. (3) A limit on parallel runs set from the server's capacity, by a system helper that checks the server (the owner said "probably": direction decided, details open). (4) Strategies can be code, AI or a mix. (5) Every strategy may have its own back-testing approach and settings (e.g. a month of old data replayed as live). (6) Protection against instructions hidden in outside text is built with live trading. (7) Agents subscribe to other agents' data; urgent data interrupts a run (a risk agent telling everyone to sell; a news worker on X posts). (8) Agents ask a workers agent for data: it knows existing workers, reuses or extends one, or creates one, and tells the agent how to use the data. (9) First strategy: one Polymarket strategy given by the owner, run the wheel, more after a good flow. (10) Real money after an agent and strategy show good results. (11) Start scale: system, domain and strategy agents plus 2-3 variants. (12) Venues and accounts chosen per strategy while it is built. (13) Workers and data from the existing Polymarket suite are reused across strategies. (14) Runs on one of the owner's servers, easy to move to a bigger one. (15) Every new strategy configuration needs a report and the owner's approval before it starts. (16) Self-improvement may change anything; agents may create workers and helpers freely for now. (17) Every action supports test and live from the start; on blockchains test can use testnets. (18) For now actions only on blockchains (any network and app); centralised exchanges and other apps are data-only. (19) Shared scripts for CRUD and filtering of the JSON lists, for agents.

Every file's page: Example is its structure, How it works answers fixed questions: On the File Tree page, a file's Example shows the structure of the file and what goes in each section (for a doc, the Outline in its skill). How it works shows only short, plain answers under fixed headings for a newcomer: What it is, Who looks after it (agent and skill), When and how it changes, Who uses it and when, Where it is mentioned, Related knowledge, Keep in mind. Questions and File stay as they are. In edit mode long lines wrap to the screen. vision.md is the first file in this format; the rule is in the knowledge base agent, the vision skill and the summary skill for every file that follows.

The README for people, built the same way as the vision: `README.md` is built the same way as `vision.md`: its own skill `readme-doc` with an Outline (shown as the README's Example on the File Tree page) and an "Its page on the File Tree" section, the doc written in plain language from every input, decision and what exists, and its How it works under the fixed headings (D-036). The README holds everything we know at overview depth and is rebuilt last in every round, with "Where things stand", "What comes next" and "Open questions" checked each time.

Markdown files open as a readable page, white or black: On the File Tree page, a Markdown file's File tab opens in a Read view: the file rendered as a page made for long reading (a text face for the body, the page's condensed face for headings, about 68 characters per line, real lists, tables and code blocks, a properties box for a skill's header), with its own white or black paper chosen in the view and remembered per viewer. It shows the word count and reading time, a contents list, and a full-screen mode with a contents sidebar, reading progress and Esc to close. Source shows the raw lines with line numbers and line comments as before; Edit works from both.

How it works in its own Markdown file, for every file and folder: The How it works of every file and folder is kept in a Markdown file of its own: `{file name}.index.md` next to a file (the full name is kept, so `run.js` and `run.py` never share one) and `{folder name}/{folder name}.index.md` inside a folder. It replaces `docs/index/summaries.json`. The File Tree page shows it on How it works and edits it like the File tab; the edit waits on the page and is written into the file at the next sync. A skill, `file-index` (replacing `knowledge-summarise`), says how to write and keep these files. The tools and the notes read and write them.

The planning project is the owner's window on the project; working from two places through GitHub: The planning project (the File Tree page, the docs, the How it works files and the knowledge behind them) is the owner's personal tool for vibecoding: to understand the project, watch it change, steer it and analyse how the system is doing, while it is planned and later while it is built and run. The owner wants it kept in the GitHub repository so the cloud project and a Claude Code on the owner's server both work on it and both know the full context.

The repository is the file tree, with the owner's IDE in project-IDE/: The GitHub repository is laid out as the file tree: `CLAUDE.md` and `README.md` at the root; `project-IDE/` with `current-ui/` (the File Tree page the owner uses now) and `data/` (the data the page needs and this project's knowledge: inputs, decisions, changelog, the tree notes, the knowledge map, the notes behind each people doc, the owner's page edits, working notes, plans, archive); `researches/`; `agents/` exactly as the tree is now, which the owner agreed as it stands ("all should be already all confirmed"); `apps/`; `trading-ui/` for the later trading dashboard. The IDE's logic lives in `agents/system/.claude/`: a new project IDE agent (builds the page from the repository, turns the owner's page notes and edits into file changes, metadata and views, runs page requests) with the skills `ide-build` (its scripts inside it) and `ide-sync`, next to the knowledge base agent and its skills; the docs for people are in `agents/system/.claude/docs/`. Every file and folder gets its `.index.md`; a file nobody has written yet exists only as its index file. Next the owner gives the GitHub project and the current tree is synced into it.

The page on the owner's server, with Claude Code behind its request box: The owner wants the File Tree page on their own server too, with the ability to run an AI agent from it that sends requests to Claude Code working in the Trading OS repository ("i would love to have on a server also ability to run ai agent that can send request to claude code connected to this trading os project").

The project IDE is one of the apps; on the server Claude Code runs from the system folder: `project-IDE/` moves into `apps/` (`apps/project-IDE/`), so `apps/` holds our own applications as well as cloned repositories. On the owner's server, Claude Code behind the page's request box starts in the system folder `agents/system/`, so the system's agents and skills load as its own and the root `CLAUDE.md` loads as its parent's. The owner asked to see the code: the four files of `apps/project-IDE/server/` are written, with the page's store kept as files in `apps/project-IDE/data/page-store/`.

Delete on the page cleans the project; one status, "changed", for now: every file and folder on the File Tree page except the top has a Delete button, with an optional note for Claude about what to keep in mind. Deleting runs the agent: on the owner's server Claude Code deletes the item and its How it works file at once, with no second click for exactly that, then cleans the project of it (its line and section in the tree notes, links, mentions in other files, the parent's How it works, the knowledge map), following the note, files it and commits; on claude.ai the item is marked deleted at once and cleaned up at the next sync. A deleted item stays in the tree, struck through, until the sync, and can be brought back the same way. The page shows no statuses for now: exists, decided, proposed, name pattern and example agent are gone from it. The one status is "changed", set on whatever a request from the page touched (an edit, a note, an added or deleted item, a request in the box, and on the server every file Claude Code changed for a request) until the next sync. More statuses may come later.

The tree lists only real files; no root CLAUDE.md or researches/; trading-ui inside apps/: the owner deleted five items on the File Tree page, each with a note. The tree shows only files and folders that will really be in the system, not examples of names: the `[name].index.md` pattern [51] and the system's `[subagent-name].md` template leave the tree (the rule that every file and folder has its How it works file stays, D-039). There is no root `CLAUDE.md` [52]: the file every Claude reads first is the system's `agents/system/.claude/CLAUDE.md` [10.1.5], which takes over its job next to the system manager prompt. There is no root `researches/` [54]: research lives inside the agents, so the prediction-market studies [54.1] go to the prediction-market domain's `research/` [19.13], and the self-improving-agents [54.2] and trading-agent architecture [54.3] studies to the system's `research/` [10.9], keeping their numbers. The example cloned repo [44] goes; `apps/` [43] holds our own apps and cloned projects, and `trading-ui/` [45] moves into it as `apps/trading-ui/`, empty for now and maybe never needed if the project IDE does its job.

An Apply changes button applies the page's changes and shows the new tree: the File Tree page has an Apply changes button at the top, with the number of items marked changed. Pressing it carries every change waiting on the page into the files and shows the new tree. On claude.ai it posts one comment on the page and sends it to Claude, which runs ide-sync and ide-build, publishes the new tree, answers the comment and resolves it; the request is also saved in the page's store, and when it turns processed the open page loads the new tree or asks the owner to reload. When no Claude is watching the page, it keeps the request and asks the owner to say "sync the file tree" in the project chat. On the owner's server it starts one Claude Code run with the same request.

An agent keeps no docs inside .claude/; .claude/docs/ moves up into the agent's own docs/: no agent keeps a `docs/` folder inside its `.claude/`. Where one exists, it moves one level up into the same agent's own `docs/`. Only the system had one: its README [2.1] and vision [2.2] now sit in `agents/system/docs/` [2], next to the topic notes agents read, and [10.1.14] is retired. The domain, strategy and trading agent `docs/` folders ([19.6], [21.6], [46]) stay where they are; a level's docs for people go there when they are written.

The vision on top, the README as the exact map of every part, and a rebuild prompt for AI: the three main docs each get one job. The vision [2.2] is the top-level doc, read first, mostly for people and for every agent's high-level view: what we are building and why, the concept, ideas, how it should work, the business logic and examples; from it the reader goes deeper. The README [2.1] is the full, long, exact overview of how the whole system works, for people and AI: a descriptive view of every main part with the path to that part's own docs, and nothing about the logic inside agents. A new third doc [2.22] is a prompt from which an AI can rebuild the system and end with the same working system, with its own skill [10.1.2.7]. The vision and README skills are rewritten to match.

The IDE and the docs give the owner and every AI the whole context: the custom IDE, the File Tree page and the docs exist so the owner can easily manage, analyse and view the system, and so AI always has all the related context it needs to make changes precisely. The docs must be right for developers and for AI. When a file changes, the AI knows which related files, agents, skills, docs, indexes and logic it has to update, and how. An AI working on a file deep in the hierarchy, such as a helper's skill, knows the knowledge from the levels above that applies to it. New knowledge from every session and every owner input is spread to where it belongs, and every question the owner asks finds its place in the docs, with an explanation of how exactly that thing works.

One job per code file; a Tests file for code, skills and agents: every code file holds one runnable thing (a function, an endpoint, a script) with one purpose. It may take different parameters, but there are no common files that mix different things: related things go in a folder, one per file, each with its own metadata. Every code file, skill, agent and subagent also gets a tests metadata file in its family, shown in a Tests tab with its own view where the owner can run a test; other files have none for now.

A plan for every change request; planning is the main development skill: every change request gets a plan before it is built, and the plan is stored. After the build, the logic in it is moved to where it belongs; later changes update the logic and knowledge in those files. Planning is a skill we define, keep and develop as the main way the system is developed.

Features as their own knowledge files, mapped both ways: some features get their own knowledge file. Features are split out, each with a map to the files it relates to, and each file maps back to its features. Small features relate to and are included in bigger ones. A feature holds the logic too detailed for the overviews (How it works, views, the README, the rebuild prompt). They live in a folder in the docs, for the system and for agents.

The vision, README and rebuild prompt as one hierarchy across levels: the vision, the README and the rebuild prompt form a hierarchy: one comes from another, and they exist for the system in general and for every domain, strategy and agent. When a lower level's docs change, the documents above are updated up to the top.

A general system, not a trading OS: the system is no longer called the Trading OS, and its top level and general knowledge know nothing about trading. Agents can be of any kind (trading, social media, management and more); each kind can share parts of the system and have its own, with its own levels below, but every agent has a parent. For trading domains the levels below are strategies and running agents.

Every app has its own docs; research clones go to a temp folder; apps we use are forked: every app in `apps/` has its own docs. A repository cloned from GitHub for research goes into a temp folder first; on request it can still get a vision, a README and a rebuild prompt. An app we use is forked, with our own main branch; from time to time the source's updates are merged in, then into our main. For now an app's metadata is only these three docs. Later, on request, a skill turns an app fully into the system's way (Details for every file, one job per file, the other docs), and that skill is kept up like every other.

The system is the Agent OS; trading lives in the prediction-market domain: the system is named the Agent OS (`agent-os`). Its top level knows nothing about trading: everything about trading moves down into the prediction-market domain, and a later trading domain is copied from it when needed. There is no folder for a kind of agent above the domains.

Metadata files are named without the file's extension; an empty metadata file for everything; a metadata switch on the page: every metadata file is named after its file without the file's extension (`vision.index.md`, `vision.meta.json`), and every file and folder gets a metadata file, empty for now. The page's `.index.md` switch becomes a "metadata" switch that shows the metadata files too.

How trading moves down: what stays general, where the trading parts go: the system level keeps only what holds for any agent: test and live modes for every outside action, the owner's approval to go live, a general stop switch, limits enforced in code that a lower level may only tighten, the key rules, outside text as data, the levels, a new version instead of a change to a running agent, self-improvement that never goes live, and cost, speed, error and test metrics. Everything about trading goes to the prediction-market domain: its own config file [19.2.4] (risk limits, trading accounts, venues, fees, market filters, the currency, the order stop switch, trade notifications), the shared buy, sell and risk scripts [14.3] (number kept), the Polymarket price collector with its logs and data, the `trading-` notes in its `docs/` [19.6], and the trading study [54.3] (number kept).

Trading is a folder of domains; trading gets its own three docs: `agents/trading/` [56] holds the trading domains: the prediction-market domain moves to `agents/trading/prediction-market/` [19] (numbers kept), and a later one is `agents/trading/copytrading/`. `agents/trading/docs/` [56.1] holds trading's own vision, README and rebuild prompt. The system's three docs are rewritten in general terms. The prediction-market and copy-trading docs are not touched now.

Voice input for the page's AI boxes, transcribed by Groq: the request box and the delete note box get a microphone button: press to record (5 minutes at most), the text is added to the box, and the owner sends it as usual. The project IDE server transcribes through Groq's free speech models (`voice.py` [53.3.5], route `api/voice`), trying the models listed in its config in order and moving on after a rate limit or an error. The key `GROQ_API_KEY` sits only in the git-ignored keys file; the page never sees it.

The research studies move to agents/trading/researches/; the page shows the real files: the repository's top-level `researches/` moves to `agents/trading/researches/` [56.2], with its three studies: prediction-market research [54.1], self-improving agents [54.2] and trading-agent architectures [54.3]. The File Tree page marks every item that exists in the repository and lists every real file under such a folder, read from the repository at each build.

An inputs vision: every owner requirement by scope, in ASD-STE100: `agents/system/docs/inputs-vision.md` [2.23] holds a detailed overview of the project from all of the owner's inputs only. Repeated logic appears once; logic a newer input contradicts is left out. It is divided by scope of logic (for example the system agent and common file rules) and written in ASD-STE100 style. Before it was written, every owner message in the project chat, its reply threads and this thread was checked against `docs/inputs/`; five messages from 2026-10-09 were missing and are now filed.

The keys folder is in git; only the .env files are not: the `.secrets/` folder, its subfolders, its How it works and Details files and `secrets.index.json` (key names only) are in git and show in the tree. Every `.env` file, which holds the key values, stays out of git. The page lists the `.env` files as local-only and never reads, shows or edits their text.

Stage one; CLAUDE.md in the system folder; the docs at five levels; README in ASD-STE100; tabs only for real files: Claude Code started in `agents/system/` reads `agents/system/CLAUDE.md`: what the project is, its stage, the reading list (project vision and README in `docs/`, system vision and README, the plain file tree `docs/file-tree.md`, the IDE docs), the current stage's work, the rules from memory, what to do after every input, and when and how each doc is updated. Every level has `docs/` with vision.md, README.md, README.asd.md (the README in ASD-STE100) and rebuild-prompt.md: the project (`docs/`), the system, trading in general, the apps, the project IDE (its README is the full IDE documentation). They are written fresh from all information and are real files, not drafts; the other docs and old drafts moved into `vision/` (`vision/docs/` and `vision/archive/2026-10-12/`). Every file and folder outside `vision/` has an `.index.md` and a `.meta.json`; the extra tab files (`x.example.md`, `x.questions.md`, `README.asd.md`; `.env.example` for a keys file) exist for the main docs and the `.env` files for now, and the page shows a tab only when its file exists. Stage one: finish the IDE, custom views, correct metadata, the docs at the project, system, trading and apps levels. Stage two: the prediction-market domain; its files moved to `vision/archive/2026-10-12/prediction-market/`, only its folders remain. New skills `readme-asd-doc` and `claude-md-doc`; the doc skills and `file-index` revised.

The tree is the files on disk; no planned items; an empty-files filter: the page and the build know only the files on disk. An item in the tree notes that is not on disk is left out of the page (enrich.py), and nothing is created from the plan any more (materialize.py now only copies drafts over their real files, copies metadata next to items, gives other items empty metadata files, keeps `.gitkeep` in empty folders and writes `docs/file-tree.md`). The page's "planned" switch and its virtual metadata rows are gone; metadata rows are the real files. A file with nothing written in it yet (0 bytes, or only `{}` / `[]`) is marked "empty", and an "empty" filter shows only those files with their folders. `vision/`, `.gitkeep` and `.env` files are never marked.

No memory folder in git; agents use the docs and the metadata: the new version keeps no memory notes in git. `vision/.claude/memory/` is deleted when `vision/` goes, not moved, and the template folder `apps/project-IDE/data/memory/` is removed. What the notes held that the docs did not: the owner's wishes (answers in ASD-STE100 when asked, low token use) go into the rules in `agents/system/CLAUDE.md`; the rule "system text stays general, money and markets go to prediction-market" goes into `agents/trading/docs/README.md`; the open questions not yet in a questions file (where `v[N]` sits in a variant name, the model defaults, the jobs) go into `agents/system/docs/README.questions.md`. History stays in the decisions and the changelog. Facts about the cloud project only stay in the cloud project memory.

The trading notes live in the prediction-market docs; the metadata logic is a top-level doc: all the trading knowledge the project has sits now in `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/`: the ten `trading-*.md` notes, `doc-outlines.md`, `trading-vision-notes.md`, `common/`, `how-to/`, `index/accounts.md`, and `README-trading-parts.md` and `rebuild-prompt-trading-parts.md` (the trading text taken out of the system docs). They are real files with their metadata, like any item; the rest of the domain stays stage two. The full logic of the metadata files, in ASD-STE100, is `docs/metadata.md`, read by every agent before it writes a metadata file and kept in step with the `file-index` skill. A found item shows its own How it works and Details on the page, read from the files next to it.

Two types of questions; the owner's questions improve the docs: every Questions file has two parts. "Open questions for the owner" holds what only the owner can answer; it is written by `change-plan` (each choice of a plan), by the new `make-questions` skill (gaps, contradictions, unapproved defaults, waiting proposals, stale answers), while a doc is written and while an item is changed; an answered question leaves it. "The owner's questions" holds each question the owner asked about the item, word for word, with its answer; it stays, and the answer is updated when it stops being true. Each owner question is also analysed for why the docs did not answer it (missing, hard to find, unclear, wrong, asked before), the docs that should have answered it are improved, and a "Docs improved" line names them (`knowledge-intake` step 6).

Questions are written in ASD-STE100; How it works and Questions tabs read like a file: everything in a Questions file is written in ASD-STE100 (open questions, reasons, recommendations, titles and answers); only the owner's own question stays word for word. The skills file-index, make-questions, change-plan and knowledge-intake and the knowledge base agent say so. On the page, How it works and Questions show their file like a Markdown file on the File tab: Read or Source, the reader controls and Full screen.

The extra knowledge notes are kept but not referenced; tree numbers and node ids go: the topic notes (overview, architecture, conventions, safety, flows, data schemas, glossary, metrics, roadmap, feature map, common, index lists) move to `apps/project-IDE/data/sources/`, and the trading notes stay in `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/`, but no doc, skill or agent refers to them; whether to use them is decided later. Knowledge goes into the level docs, CLAUDE.md, metadata.md and each item's metadata files. The tree numbers and node ids of the old tree notes are not needed once the path is the id: `tree_number` is removed from every Details file now; the numbers and ids leave the How it works front matter, the knowledge tags and the page in the move out of `vision/`.

Go for the move out of vision/; fill every Details field first; one set of decision statuses: the move out of `vision/` starts, in one pull request, and removes `vision/archive/` (git history keeps it). Its first step fills every field of every Details file outside `vision/` from the item, its docs and the knowledge still in `vision/`; no field is dropped. Decisions have one of three statuses: decided, proposed or replaced ("decided. Partly replaced by ..." for a part). The stage-one defaults (the name `rebuild-prompt.md`, the prediction-market folder names, the project docs in the top `docs/`) are accepted. PR #5 is merged into main.

# agent-os/

## What it is

The whole repository of the Agent OS: the owner's system that runs AI agents of any kind, such as trading, social media or management. Trading is the first kind; it lives in `agents/trading/`, whose first domain, prediction-market, waits for stage two. The project is in stage one: finish the project IDE, make every metadata file correct and finish the docs at the project, system, trading and apps levels.

The top holds `docs/`, the project docs for people (vision, README and its ASD-STE100 twin, rebuild prompt, the plain file tree and the metadata logic); `agents/`, with the system level in `agents/system/` (its `CLAUDE.md` is the file AI sessions read first) and trading in `agents/trading/`; `apps/`, with the project IDE (the owner's File Tree page and the project's records), the trading dashboard and research clones; `.secrets/`, the keys store, in git except its `.env` files; `README.md`, the front page, empty for now; `HANDOFF.md`, how a new session picks the work up; and `.gitignore`. The old planning folder `vision/` is removed; git history keeps it. Every file and folder has a How it works file and a Details file next to it.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner; knowledge-base-agent; and project-ide-agent (ide-sync, ide-build).

## When and how it changes

It changes when a top-level folder or file is added, moved or removed, or the stage or the way of working changes.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner, every agent, Claude Code started in agents/system/ and an AI rebuilding the repository.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `docs/README.md`, `docs/vision.md` and `docs/file-tree.md`.

## Related knowledge

## Keep in mind

- When anything needs a secret, list the key name in `secret_keys` and let `load-secret` load it; never write a value anywhere.

# .secrets/live/.env: the key names this file holds, with no values.
# The real .env stays on the machine and never goes in git. Type real values only there.

# Which secrets file load-secret reads: test or live. test | live, required. Used by load-secret.
AGENT_OS_ENV=live

# Claude API for agents and sub-agents run headless. sk-ant-..., required. Used by run-agent, run-lives.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# Polymarket CLOB API key for test account 1. uuid, required. Used by acct-pm-live-1, polymarket-exec.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY=

# Secret paired with the API key. base64, required. Used by acct-pm-live-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_SECRET=

# Passphrase paired with the API key. text, required. Used by acct-pm-live-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_PASSPHRASE=

# Signs orders for the account's wallet. 0x + 64 hex, required. Used by acct-pm-live-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=

# Alerts to Telegram (later). 123:ABC..., optional. Used by notifier.
NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=

The test side of the keys store. It holds `.env`, git-ignored, meant for every test key; `.env.example`, its key names with no values; and the metadata files of the keys file. Agents may read and update the test keys because they are safe test credentials.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a file is added to or removed from the test side of the keys store.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner; and load-secret (the proposed shared loader, not written yet).

It is described in `agents/system/docs/README.md` and its folder's How it works file `.secrets/.secrets.index.md`.

example.body:
# .secrets/test/.env: the key names this file holds, with no values.
# The real .env stays on the machine and never goes in git. Type real values only there.

# Which secrets file load-secret reads: test or live. test | live, required. Used by load-secret.
AGENT_OS_ENV=test

# Claude API for agents and sub-agents run headless. sk-ant-..., required. Used by run-agent, run-tests.
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=

# Polymarket CLOB API key for test account 1. uuid, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1, polymarket-exec.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY=

# Secret paired with the API key. base64, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_SECRET=

# Passphrase paired with the API key. text, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_PASSPHRASE=

# Signs orders for the account's wallet. 0x + 64 hex, required. Used by acct-pm-test-1.
POLYMARKET_ACCT1_WALLET_PRIVATE_KEY=

# Groq speech to text for voice input in the project IDE (D-060); test file only. gsk_..., optional. Used by apps/project-IDE/server/voice.py.
GROQ_API_KEY=

# Other models via OpenRouter (not connected yet). sk-or-..., optional. Used by models.config.json.
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=

# Alerts to Telegram (later). 123:ABC..., optional. Used by notifier.
NOTIFY_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=

# .env

## What it is

The file meant to hold every test credential as `KEY=value` lines, grouped in comment sections (mode, models, platforms and accounts, notifications), with names that start with their account or platform, such as `POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY`. It is git-ignored and stays on the machine; its key names, with no values, are in `.env.example` next to it. The project IDE server reads its keys from it by name. Agents and the dev workflow may read and update it, since these are safe test keys.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a test key is added, renamed, removed or given a new value. It is empty for now.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by load-secret (the proposed shared loader, not written yet); and scripts that list the key in secret_keys.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `.secrets/secrets.index.json` and its folder's How it works file `.secrets/test/test.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It has the same format as `.secrets/test/.env.example` and `.secrets/live/.env`. It is checked by `.gitignore`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md`, `docs/README.md` (section "Keys and secrets") and `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Keys and secrets").

## Keep in mind

- When you add a test key, put it in the matching section with its account or platform prefix and add the same name to `live/.env` and `secrets.index.json`.
- When a config or job needs a key, list its name in `secret_keys`; never copy the value anywhere else.

# Questions: .env

## Open questions for the owner

- **Which machine holds this file: only the owner's server, or also a laptop?** The answer decides where the owner types the keys. It also decides where the backup is.

- **Is one test account sufficient for stage one?** The IDE can need more keys, for example for a second model platform.

- When a key is added, renamed or removed in an `.env` file, update its entry here in the same change, with no value.

how.text:
All agents of the Agent OS, one folder per domain. The system is a domain too: `system/` holds the system agent and everything every agent shares, whatever its domain. `trading/` is a folder of trading domains with trading's own docs; its first domain, `trading/prediction-market/`, holds everything about trading today, and the next, `trading/copytrading/`, will be copied from it. Inside the prediction-market domain sit its strategy agents, and inside each strategy its trading agents, one per version being tested.

Every level uses one identical agent folder: `.claude/` with the level's prompt, then `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/` and the level files. Each content folder holds the level's own files, file links to what it reads elsewhere, and `subagents.link/` to its children. Agents are created by `create-agent`, and self-improvement creates new test versions. Secrets, the apps and cloned code live outside this folder.
keep: When you add an agent, give it a unique name and the standard folder through `create-agent`; never copy a folder by hand.
When an agent needs another agent's file, add a link to its links file; it never writes into another agent's folder.

# agents/

## What it is

All agents of the Agent OS, one folder per domain. The system is a domain too: `system/` holds the system agent and everything every agent shares, whatever its domain. `trading/` is a folder of trading domains with trading's own docs; its first domain, `trading/prediction-market/`, holds everything about trading today, and the next, `trading/copytrading/`, will be copied from it. Inside the prediction-market domain sit its strategy agents, and inside each strategy its trading agents, one per version being tested.

Every level uses one identical agent folder: `.claude/` with the level's prompt, then `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/`, `research/` and the level files. Each content folder holds the level's own files, file links to what it reads elsewhere, and `subagents.link/` to its children. Agents are created by `create-agent`, and self-improvement creates new test versions. Secrets, the apps and cloned code live outside this folder.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner, knowledge-base-agent and project-ide-agent (ide-sync).

## When and how it changes

It changes when a domain or an agent level is added, moved or removed.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner, every agent and Claude Code started in agents/system/.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `docs/README.md`, `agents/system/docs/README.md`, `agents/trading/docs/README.md`, `docs/file-tree.md` and its folder's How it works file `agent-os.index.md`.

how.text:
The system level of the Agent OS: the system agent and the home of everything every agent shares, whatever its domain. Like every level it has the standard agent folder; its agent, the system manager, oversees the domains, the system's health and its development, and answers the owner's questions about the whole system. `CLAUDE.md` here is the file Claude Code reads first.

Its folders hold what holds for any agent: `configs/` the global settings (test or live, the live list, the general stop switch, jobs, links) and model routing; `scripts/` the shared machinery (create-agent, the scheduler, relink, load-secret, run-tests) and collectors shared by several domains, all still planned; `logs/` and `data/` the shared logs and outputs; `tests/` and `research/`; `docs/` the system's vision, README, README twin and rebuild prompt. Its `.claude/` holds the settings, the skills and the helpers: self-improvement, the knowledge base agent and the project IDE agent.

Agents are meant to use shared files through read-only file links, never copies, and the system reaches each domain through `subagents.link/`, one level at a time. Trading lives in `agents/trading/`, not here.
keep: When agents of different domains need the same agent-local thing, move it into the matching shared folder here and give each a file link; what one domain needs stays in that domain.
When a rule or setting holds only for one domain, put it in that domain, not here.
When an owner input or a system change comes in, run it through the knowledge base agent so the docs and the metadata files stay current.

# system/

## What it is

The system level of the Agent OS: the system agent and the home of everything every agent shares, whatever its domain. Like every level it has the standard agent folder; its agent, the system manager, oversees the domains, the system's health and its development, and answers the owner's questions about the whole system. `CLAUDE.md` here is the file Claude Code reads first.

Its folders hold what holds for any agent: `configs/` the global settings (test or live, the live list, the general stop switch, jobs, links) and model routing; `scripts/` the shared machinery (create-agent, the scheduler, relink, load-secret, run-tests) and collectors shared by several domains, all still planned; `logs/` and `data/` the shared logs and outputs; `tests/` and `research/`; `docs/` the system's vision, README, README twin and rebuild prompt. Its `.claude/` holds the settings, the skills and the helpers: self-improvement, the knowledge base agent and the project IDE agent.

Agents are meant to use shared files through read-only file links, never copies, and the system reaches each domain through `subagents.link/`, one level at a time. Trading lives in `agents/trading/`, not here.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner; knowledge-base-agent; project-ide-agent; and relink (planned shared script in agents/system/scripts/system/), for the child links.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a shared part is added, moved or removed, or a domain is added or removed and its child links change.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner; every Claude Code session started in agents/system/; the system agent; every agent, through file links to the shared files; and `agents/system/.claude/skills/ide-build/scripts/enrich.py`.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/README.md`, `agents/system/docs/vision.md`, `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`, `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` and `agents/agents.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It links to `agents/trading/prediction-market/`. It reads `.secrets/`. The rules that apply to it come from `docs/vision.md`, `docs/README.md` (section "The system"), `docs/metadata.md` and `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules").

## Keep in mind

- When agents of different domains need the same agent-local thing, move it into the matching shared folder here and give each a file link; what one domain needs stays in that domain.
- When a rule or setting holds only for one domain, put it in that domain, not here.
- When an owner input or a system change comes in, run it through the knowledge base agent so the docs and the metadata files stay current.

# .claude/

## What it is

The system level's Claude Code folder, laid out the same way at every level. It holds the settings (`settings.json`, and `settings.local.json` for one machine), the skills in `skills/`, the helper agents in `agents/` (the self-improvement agent, the knowledge base agent and the project IDE agent), the sub-agents' memory folders, and `rules/`, `commands/`, `output-styles/` and `workflows/`, which hold only name patterns for now. ## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner, knowledge-base-agent, project-ide-agent and change-plan.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a helper agent, a skill, a setting or one of the standard parts is added, changed or removed.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by Claude Code started in agents/system/, knowledge-base-agent, project-ide-agent and the owner.

## Where it is mentioned

## Keep in mind

nodes.name: knowledge-base-agent.md
nodes.summary: The knowledge base agent: keeps every input and what we know, and writes the docs and every metadata file.
nodes.purpose: The knowledge base agent: keeps every input and what we know, and writes the docs and every metadata file.

how.text: The knowledge base agent: the project's librarian and writer. It saves every owner message, every answer we give, every change to the system and what a session learned, so nothing gets lost or contradicts itself. From those notes it writes the docs in plain, book-like language, each with that doc's own skill, and keeps the three main docs in line after every update: the vision first, then the README, then the rebuild prompt for AI. The docs are also the context every AI works from, so they must be exact enough to act on: for any file, what it is for, how it works, what depends on it and what holds for it from the levels above. It also keeps the How it works file of every file and folder. The File Tree page itself is looked after by the project IDE agent.
keep: When you write any doc, write for a reader who is not technical: no reference numbers, codes or ids.
When you mark something decided, make sure the owner said it; otherwise it is an idea or an open question.
When the owner asks a question, write the answer where they should have found it.

# knowledge-base-agent.md

## What it is

The knowledge base agent: the project's librarian and writer. It saves every owner message, every answer we give, every change to the system and what a session learned, so nothing gets lost or contradicts itself. From those notes it writes the docs in plain, book-like language, each with that doc's own skill, and keeps the three main docs in line after every update: the vision first, then the README, then the rebuild prompt for AI. The docs are also the context every AI works from, so they must be exact enough to act on: for any file, what it is for, how it works, what depends on it and what holds for it from the levels above. It also keeps the How it works file of every file and folder. The File Tree page itself is looked after by the project IDE agent.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner and knowledge-base-agent with knowledge-intake.

## When and how it changes

It changes when the owner changes how knowledge is kept or how a doc is written, or a skill of the agent is added or renamed.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by Claude Code started in agents/system/ (as a helper) and the owner.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/README.md` and its folder's How it works file `agents/system/.claude/agents/agents.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It reads `agents/system/.claude/skills/knowledge-intake/SKILL.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/file-index/SKILL.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/vision-doc/SKILL.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/readme-doc/SKILL.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/readme-asd-doc/SKILL.md`, `agents/system/.claude/skills/rebuild-prompt-doc/SKILL.md` and `agents/system/.claude/skills/claude-md-doc/SKILL.md`. It links to `agents/system/.claude/agents/project-ide-agent.md`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "When and how to update each doc"), `docs/metadata.md` and `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "The knowledge base and the docs").

## Keep in mind

- When you write any doc, write for a reader who is not technical: no reference numbers, codes or ids.
- When you mark something decided, make sure the owner said it; otherwise it is an idea or an open question.
- When the owner asks a question, write the answer where they should have found it.

# sys-self-improvement-agent.md

## What it is

The system's self-improvement helper: it improves the system itself (shared scripts, shared configs, model routing and shared docs) and reacts to new models and tools. It runs as a nightly job in `configs/system.workers.json`, reads errors and costs in the system's logs, the domains through `subagents.link/`, owner comments and outside news, and writes research items to `research/` and proposals marked pending owner. Its file template, memory place and outputs are proposals.

## Who looks after it

It is written by knowledge-base-agent, when the owner asks for it to be written.

## When and how it changes

It changes when its instructions are first written, or its scope, limits or job change. It is empty for now.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by Claude Code started in agents/system/ (as a helper) and the system's jobs file (its switched-off job).

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/README.md` and its folder's How it works file `agents/system/.claude/agents/agents.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It writes `agents/system/.claude/agent-memory/` and `agents/system/research/`. It reads `agents/system/configs/models.config.json`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md`, `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Each agent's AI setup"), `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md` (section "The standard .claude/ folder") and `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Self-improvement helpers").

## Keep in mind

- When you try a change, make it a new test version; never edit a running agent, touch live agents, loosen a limit or read `.secrets/live/`.
- When you want to change a shared file, record it as a proposal marked pending owner instead of applying it.
- When you set its model, set it in its job or in `configs/models.config.json`, not in this file.

how.text: The main development skill: every change request gets a plan before anything is built. A request from the owner, from the File Tree page or from an agent that wants to improve the system becomes one plan file, named by the request's date, time and subject. The plan says what was asked, what it is for, what exists today, the change part by part with examples, the choices for the owner with a recommended default, the steps with a check for each, everything it touches, and where each piece of its knowledge will live once built. The owner sees it before the build. After the build, its knowledge moves into the files that own it, the docs are brought in line from the vision down, and the plan is archived. Questions and small fixes, such as a typo or a rebuild of the page, need no plan. Proposed, written on the owner's request.
keep: When a change request arrives, save the owner's words first, then write the plan before you build anything.
When the build is done, move every piece of the plan's knowledge to its home and archive the plan; never leave knowledge only in a plan.
When a later change touches the same thing, start from the files that hold the knowledge now, not from the archived plan.

# file-index/SKILL.md

## What it is

The instructions the knowledge base agent follows to write and keep the How it works file of every file and folder: where each file goes and how it is named (after its file without the extension, so `vision.md` has `vision.index.md`), its fixed headings, how long it is, and how to write it in plain words for someone new to the project.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent keeps it up to date. Whatever the owner decides about how How it works should look or read goes into it.

## When and how it changes

When the owner changes how How it works should look or read, or how it is kept. The agent updates the skill, then refreshes the index files the change touches.

## Who uses it, and when

The knowledge base agent, after every input or change, once the docs are updated: it lists the out-of-date index files, deepest first, and rewrites or confirms each one. At every sync it also writes the owner's edits from the File Tree page into the files.

## Where it is mentioned

The knowledge base agent's instructions, the last steps of the skill that files every input, the page sections of the vision and README skills, and the file tree.

## Related knowledge

- The index files themselves, one per file and folder.
- Each doc skill's page section, which says what goes under each heading for that doc.
- The map of knowledge to files, which says what each index file is written from.

## Keep in mind

- When you change the headings or the rules here, refresh every index file they touch, deepest first.
- When an index file is still right, confirm it instead of rewriting it, so its parents do not go out of date for nothing.

## What it is

Lists the items of the tree from the repository: every file git keeps, the folders that hold them and the local keys files, with the top as `agent-os`. ## The owner's questions

### 2026-10-13: How does the tree stay the same as the disk?

> explain me in ads style how de we sync file tree with a disk step by step

The page has no tree of its own. After a change, the build does these steps:

1. `enrich.py` reads each file that git keeps, with its metadata. It marks the empty files.
2. `materialize.py` gives empty metadata files to new items. It keeps a `.gitkeep` in empty folders. It writes `docs/file-tree.md`.
3. `build_map.py` checks the How it works files.
4. `check_page.js` tests the page.
5. The build compares the page tree with git.
6. The build publishes the page.

The owner can make a change on the page. That change goes to the disk first through `ide-sync`, after Apply changes.

### 2026-10-05: How do notes and comments on the page become agent work?

> also not clear how we now hanlding agentic works from the ui comments and notes on files and folders?

The page saves each thing that you leave on it at once, in the store of the page. It marks the item "changed".

You push Apply changes or say "sync the file tree". Then this skill does these steps:

1. It records each message as an owner input, word for word.
2. It writes the edits into their files.
3. It applies the notes that are changes. It makes the other open notes into open questions.
4. It does the requests.
5. It completes the deletions.
6. It gives the inputs to the knowledge base agent.
7. It builds the page again with `ide-build`.

On the owner's server, the page writes the edits into the files at once. A request starts Claude Code immediately.

# Questions: SKILL.md

## Open questions for the owner

None open.

## The owner's questions

### 2026-10-05: Does a question with its answer update the knowledge?

> telll me for example i have question you answer me do we update any knowledge from that?

Yes. The agent stores the question and its answer together as one owner input, word for word. It also records them in the Questions file of the item that the question is about.

The answer can add a new fact. Then the agent also writes that fact in these locations:

1. The docs.
2. The decisions.
3. The changelog.
4. The metadata of the items that the fact is about.

The agent also writes the answer into the doc where the owner looked for it.

It also reads the owner's own past questions: many questions on one item show a weak doc, and the skill improves that doc before it asks anything. Each question it writes goes into the item's Questions file, part "Open questions for the owner", with one sentence on why it matters and a recommended answer, at most five per item. Then it tells the owner the count and the most important ones, and rebuilds the page.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner and knowledge-base-agent.

## When and how it changes

It changes when the owner changes how open questions are found, written or answered.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by knowledge-base-agent, change-plan and every AI that finishes a doc or a plan.

# configs/

## What it is

The system's settings folder. It holds the settings that hold for every agent, the choice of AI model for every agent, the system agent's own jobs and links, and one link to each domain's settings folder. All of it is plain JSON files people can open and edit.

## Who looks after it

The system's support helpers write the shared settings; the owner changes jobs from the File Tree page and approves changes to the modes, the stop switch and the live list.

## When and how it changes

When a system-wide setting, a model choice, a system job or a system link changes; and when a domain is added or removed, which adds or removes its link.

## Who uses it, and when

Every agent at the start of each run reads the shared settings and the model choice through its own links; the scheduler reads the jobs; the File Tree page shows all of it.

## Where it is mentioned

Every agent's own settings folder, which has the same kind of files; each domain's own config; the rules for merging settings; the File Tree page.

## Related knowledge

- Settings merge from here, then the domain's config, then the agent's own, then the owner's overrides; a lower layer may only tighten a limit.
- Each agent keeps its own settings, jobs and links in its own settings folder; only what every agent shares lives here.
- The exact shape of the files, and which settings are shared, are still open.

## Keep in mind

- When a setting applies to one agent or one domain only, put it in that agent's or domain's own settings, not here.
- When a key is needed, list its name only; never write its value.

Every level has the same kind of folder in each of its own folders, so each level sees the one below it. The links are read-only.

## Keep in mind

- When you need a domain's settings, read them through this folder; never copy them into the system's folder.

# system.config.json

## What it is

The one file of settings that hold for the whole system and every agent: default values, test or live mode with the list of agents allowed to act live, the general stop switch, schedule defaults, what counts as an important change, and notifications. Jobs and the choice of AI model are kept in their own files, and a domain's own settings, such as the prediction-market domain's trading settings, in that domain's config.

## Who looks after it

The system's support helpers write it. Changes to the modes, the stop switch and the live list need the owner's approval.

## When and how it changes

When a setting for the whole system changes. A section that grows long moves into a file of its own.

## Who uses it, and when

Every agent at the start of each run, merged with its domain's settings and its own into the settings it actually uses. Every script that acts checks the stop switch before each action; the File Tree page shows the values.

## Where it is mentioned

Each agent's own settings file and its link to this file, each domain's own config, the rules for merging settings, the safety rules and the File Tree page.

## Related knowledge

- A lower level's settings can only make a limit stricter, never looser.
- No agent can switch itself to live: live needs the live list here, the owner's approval and the stop switch off.
- The sections and their fields are still a proposal.

## Keep in mind

- When you add a setting, put it here only if it holds for every agent; a domain's setting goes in the domain's config, one agent's in its own.
- When you change the modes, the stop switch or the live list, get the owner's approval first.
- When a key is needed, write only its name, never its value.

# system.links.json

## What it is

The list of the files the system agent links in from other folders: for each link, which file, from where, where it appears and why. It also sets the format every agent uses for its own list. The system's list is short; most links belong to the agents at the lowest levels.

## Who looks after it

The script that creates agents writes the first version. After that the agent itself, its self-improvement helper and the owner edit it.

## When and how it changes

When the agent needs a file from somewhere else, or no longer needs one. Relink then turns the list into links.

## Who uses it, and when

Relink and the link check read it every time they run; the index of all links and the File Tree page show who links what.

## Where it is mentioned

The links files of every other agent, the rules for links, and the relink script.

## Related knowledge

- Links point at single files only, never at keys and never into an AI setup folder.
- Child links are not listed here; relink makes them from the folders.
- Still open: whether the links themselves are saved in git or rebuilt after every download.

## Keep in mind

- When you add or change a link, edit this list and run relink; never make a link by hand.
- When a link would point at a key or into an AI setup folder, don't add it.

In the Agent OS none of these holds the list: every job is written in its agent's jobs file, and the one scheduler, planned to run on the owner's server, starts it.

# system.workers.json

## What it is

The list of everything the system agent itself runs, on a schedule or on demand: relinking and link checks, tests, index rebuilds, data collectors shared by several domains, its helpers' runs, and the knowledge base agent's regular sync. Each job is either a plain script or an AI run, and says whether it is on, when it runs, where, and with which AI model. Every agent has a file just like it.

## Who looks after it

The owner, from the File Tree page: turning jobs on or off and changing when, where and with which model they run. The system's helpers propose changes. For now every job is off (the owner, 2026-10-09): they stay in the file and run only once turned on.

## When and how it changes

Only when someone adds, changes, pauses or removes a job. What actually happened when a job ran is kept elsewhere, so the file does not change with every run.

## Who uses it, and when

The scheduler reads it to start each job at its time; the File Tree page and the list of all jobs show it.

## Where it is mentioned

The jobs files of every other agent, which use the same format; the list of all jobs; the scheduler.

## Related knowledge

- A live job needs the owner's approval and an agent on the live list.
- Jobs that run in the cloud, on the desktop or on GitHub get no keys and never act live.
- The exact fields are a proposal.
- Claude Code itself can also run work on a schedule: `/loop` in an open session, cloud routines kept in the Claude account, scheduled tasks of the desktop app, GitHub Actions with a `schedule:` line, or the machine's cron or systemd timer running `claude -p`. In the Agent OS none of these holds the list: every job is written in its agent's jobs file, and the one scheduler, planned to run on the owner's server, starts it.

## Keep in mind

- When you want to pause a job, turn it off; never delete it to pause it.
- When a job would act live, get the owner's approval first.

### 2026-09-30: How do scheduled jobs work in Claude Code?

> how in a claude code we do scheduled jobs and where do they stored? tell me more how it works

Claude Code has five methods:

1. `/loop` in an open session.

Today all system jobs are off. The scheduler is not built yet.

# system/

## What it is

The system's own state files, the runtime memory of the shared machinery. `scheduler-state.json` holds every job's last run, result, next run and failure count; only the scheduler writes it, so workers files never change at run time. `links.index.json` lists every link in the project (owner agent, where it appears, real target, required, status); only relink writes it, and the UI, `check-links` and the runbooks read it to see who reads which file. Both formats are proposed. Still open: whether a `run-state.json` with per-agent read cursors is needed, which depends on how "new since the last run" is tracked.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the scheduler (planned), for its record of jobs; and relink (planned), for the list of links.

## When and how it changes

At run time, when a job runs or a link changes; the folder changes only when a record is added or its format changes. It is empty for now.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by check-links (planned); the system agent; and the owner, on the File Tree page.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Jobs and the scheduler"), `agents/system/data/` and its folder's How it works file `agents/system/data/data.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It is written by `agents/system/scripts/system/`. It is built from `agents/system/configs/system.workers.json` and `agents/system/configs/system.links.json`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md`, `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Workers and data") and `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "Jobs and the scheduler").

## Keep in mind

- When you need these files changed, let their one writer do it: the scheduler for `scheduler-state.json`, relink for `links.index.json`.
- When you move or delete a file others read, check `links.index.json` for its readers first.

# docs/

## What it is

The system domain's docs: four docs about the system, read in order. `vision.md` says why and how the system should work; `README.md` maps every part exactly with the path to its docs; `README.asd.md` is the README again in ASD-STE100 for the owner to compare; `rebuild-prompt.md` is the spec an AI rebuilds `agents/system/` from. The knowledge base agent writes the four docs; the owner can edit them on the File Tree page; `relink` makes the child links.

After every owner input or change that touches the system, the docs are updated in the order vision, README, README.asd, rebuild prompt.

The owner, every Claude that works on the system (through `CLAUDE.md`'s reading list), and the system manager when it reads its domains' docs through `subagents.link/`.

`agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (Read first, and the table of docs); the project's README; the rebuild prompts of the project and of the system.

# [domain-name]/

## What it is

One folder link per domain, named after the domain's folder and pointing at that domain's own `docs/`, so the system can read the domain's docs, and from there those of the levels below it, without copies. It is read-only: the system writes only its own docs. `relink` builds it from the folder tree and removes it when the domain is gone; it is never listed in a links file.

## Who looks after it

It is written by relink (planned shared script in agents/system/scripts/system/), when a domain is added; never by hand.

## When and how it changes

Only when a domain is added or removed; relink makes or deletes the link. It is a name pattern, not a real item: it tells what each item made from it will hold.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the system agent; the owner, on the File Tree page; sys-self-improvement-agent; and knowledge-base-agent.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/subagents.link/`, `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "How a level reaches its children") and its folder's How it works file `agents/system/docs/subagents.link/subagents.link.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It links to `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md` and `agents/system/docs/README.md` (section "How a level reaches its children").

## Keep in mind

- When you need a domain's docs, read them through this link; never write into it.
- When a domain is added or removed, let `relink` make or remove this link; never create it by hand.

## What it is

The system's README again, in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. It has the same content and the same section order as `README.md`, in short sentences: descriptive ones at most 25 words, procedural ones at most 20, active voice, present tense, one word for one meaning, numbered steps for procedures. The knowledge base agent writes it right after the README. The planned skill `readme-asd-doc` will hold its rules; until it exists, the rules are in the README's own skill and in this note.

It changes every time `README.md` changes. The agent rewrites the matching sections and checks sentence and paragraph lengths. It never adds a fact the README does not have.

The owner reads it to compare with the README and to check that the README says things clearly. Agents read the README, not this file.

- When the two differ, `README.md` is correct: fix this file.
- When you write here, use the README's names exactly; do not invent synonyms.

# README.md

## What it is

The system's README: an exact map of the system domain for people. It describes every part of `agents/system/` and what it shares with every agent, in a fixed order (agents and levels, the system agent and shared files, domains, workers, jobs, links, settings and models, test and live, keys, logs, tests, research, self-improvement, the AI setup, the knowledge base, the project IDE, the server), and ends each part with the path to its docs.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent writes it with the `readme-doc` skill. The owner can also change it on the File Tree page.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a part changes: a folder, an agent, a config, a job, a script, or how parts connect. The agent rewrites that part's section and the overview, then rewrites `README.asd.md` right after and brings the rebuild prompt in line.

## Who uses it, and when

The owner reads it to see how the system is built. `CLAUDE.md` puts it fourth in its reading list, so every Claude reads it before it changes the system. Domain agents read it to learn what they share.

## Where it is mentioned

`agents/system/CLAUDE.md` lists it under Read first; the project's README points to it for the system; the vision's last section points to it; `README.asd.md` names it as its source.

## Related knowledge

Its ASD-STE100 version `README.asd.md` follows it section for section. The vision gives the why; the rebuild prompt gives the same parts as an exact spec. Trading's README (`agents/trading/docs/README.md`) and the IDE's README (`apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`) cover the levels it points to.

## Keep in mind

- When you change a section here, rewrite the same section in `README.asd.md` in the same round.
- When a part's docs move, fix its "Its docs:" line.
- When you describe a setting that is not decided, mark it proposed or open.
