# Trading (ASD-STE100)

This file is the ASD-STE100 version of `README.md` in this folder. `README.md` is the source. If the two files do not agree, use `README.md`.

## In short

Trading is the first type of work in the Agent OS. All of the trading work is in one folder. This folder contains the trading domains, the trading docs and the trading research.

A trading domain is one area of trading, for example prediction markets. Each trading domain operates many small trading agents at the same time. Each idea starts in test mode, with no real money. The system keeps the versions that work. Only the owner can give real money to an agent.

The first trading domain is prediction markets on Polymarket. A new trading domain starts as a copy of the prediction-market domain. Then it changes only its own parts.

The system level stays general. The docs, settings and scripts of the system contain no information about money, markets or orders. All of this information is in trading and in its domains.

Status: the trading docs and the research studies exist. The prediction-market domain has empty folders. Its `docs/` folder contains earlier notes. They are kept for stage two. Its other old files are in an archive. The project writes this domain again in stage two. No part that trades exists at this time.

This document gives a full and exact description of each part of `agents/trading/`. It also tells what each trading domain contains, and where the docs of each part are. It does not tell how an agent makes decisions. The vision, `agents/trading/docs/vision.md`, tells why trading has its own folder, how trading must operate and the rules.

## Trading at a glance

`agents/trading/` is a folder. It is not an agent. It has no AI instructions, no settings, no scripts and no jobs. It has no `.claude/` folder. Each file and each folder in it has a How it works file and a Details file.

| Part | Purpose | Location |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's docs | Tell what all trading domains share, how to make a new domain and how to build this folder again | `agents/trading/docs/` |
| Research studies | Give the start information for the trading domains | `agents/trading/researches/` |
| Prediction-market domain | The first trading domain. Stage two. At this time: folders and earlier notes | `agents/trading/prediction-market/` |
| Later trading domains | Copies of the prediction-market domain. The owner asks for them | `agents/trading/[domain]/`. None at this time |
| Trading dashboard | The dashboard of the prediction-market domain. Empty | `apps/trading-ui/` |

How the parts connect:

1. The system agent connects to each trading domain directly, through its child links. This folder does not add a level of agents.
2. A domain agent uses the research studies and the ideas of the owner to start its strategies.
3. In a domain, information goes down. Workers collect prices and other data into the `data/` folder of the domain. Each strategy and each trading agent links the files that it needs.
4. Trading agents write their decisions and orders to logs. Their results go up, level by level, to the domain agent and to the dashboard of the owner.
5. The owner approves new trading agents and real money. The owner can stop each trading agent.

## How trading is laid out

```
agents/trading/
├── trading.index.md / trading.meta.json   How it works and Details of this folder
├── docs/                                  trading's own docs
│   ├── vision.md                          why trading, what all trading domains share
│   ├── README.md                          the source of this file
│   ├── README.asd.md                      this file
│   └── rebuild-prompt.md                  how an AI builds this folder again
├── researches/                            the research studies
│   ├── prediction-market-research/        ways to make money on prediction markets
│   ├── self-improving-agents/             agents that make themselves better
│   └── trding-agents-arhiteches/          how trading agents are built
└── prediction-market/                     the first trading domain (stage two)
```

Each trading domain uses the standard agent folder at each of its three levels:

```
[agent folder]/
├── .claude/          the AI setup of the agent: rules, skills, commands, sub-agents, workflows, output styles, memory
├── configs/          settings, jobs and links files, and links to shared settings
├── scripts/          the scripts of the agent, and links to shared scripts
├── logs/             run logs and session logs
├── data/             the data that the workers of the agent collect, and links to shared data
├── docs/             vision.md, README.md, rebuild-prompt.md and the notes of the agent
├── tests/            agents/ (tests of instructions) and scripts/ (tests of scripts)
├── research/         one folder for each research item
└── [child agent]/    the agents one level below
```

A level with children has a `subagents.link/` folder in each content folder. The content folders are `configs/`, `scripts/`, `logs/`, `data/`, `docs/`, `tests/` and `research/`. `subagents.link/` contains one folder link for each child. Each link goes to the folder of the same type in that child. A trading agent has no children. Thus it has no `subagents.link/` folder.

## The parts

### Trading's docs

`agents/trading/docs/` contains the trading docs. People and AI read them. The docs are:

- `vision.md`: why trading has its own folder, what all trading domains share and how to make a new domain.
- `README.md`: the full description of the parts.
- `README.asd.md`: this file. It is `README.md` in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Use it to compare the two texts.
- `rebuild-prompt.md`: the prompt that an AI uses to build this folder again.

Each doc has a How it works file and a Details file. Each doc also has an outline file (`[name].example.md`) and a file of open questions (`[name].questions.md`).

These docs are between the system docs above and the docs of each trading domain below. They tell only what all trading domains share. The details of one domain stay in the docs of that domain. If a change in a domain affects all domains, update these docs. Then update the system docs above them.

The knowledge base agent writes these docs. It uses the skills `vision-doc`, `readme-doc`, `readme-asd-doc` (planned) and `rebuild-prompt-doc`. The owner can also change the docs on the File Tree page.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md`

### Research studies

`agents/trading/researches/` contains the research studies. These are real files. They existed before the trading agents. The folder keeps the name `researches/` that the owner gave it. The research history of each agent is in the `research/` folder of that agent.

- `prediction-market-research/`: 42 studies of ways to make money on prediction markets. The numbers are `01` to `34` and `50` to `57`. Each study is one Markdown file, for example `01-maker-reward-pool-farming.md`. Some studies describe practices that you must not do, for example wash trading and insider trading. `_evidence/` contains the background evidence `E1` to `E9`, the strategy lists and one row for each study. `_pipeline/` contains the pipeline that wrote the studies.
- `self-improving-agents/`: one study of methods and architectures for agents that make themselves better.
- `trding-agents-arhiteches/`: one study of how trading agents are built. It contains `README.md`, 9 architecture specifications in `specs/`, their diagrams in `diagrams/` and a gallery page `index.html`.

The domain agents read these studies when they look for strategies. The owner reads them on the File Tree page. Do not change a study after it is complete. If a study causes a decision, record the decision in the notes.

Its docs: `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md`

### The trading domains

Each trading domain is a full domain of the Agent OS. Each domain has its own folder in `agents/trading/`. Each domain is a direct child of the system agent. Each domain has three levels of agents. Each level uses the standard agent folder:

- **The domain agent** is in the folder of the domain. It finds, makes and updates strategies. It makes sure that the domain makes money. It answers the questions of the owner.
- **Strategy agents** each have one folder in the domain, for example `strategy-1-agent/`. Each strategy agent owns one way to make money, its definition and its versions.
- **Trading agents** (variants) each have one folder in their strategy. They are the versions that trade.

**The prediction-market domain** (`agents/trading/prediction-market/`) is the first domain. It trades on Polymarket first. At this time it contains only folders. Each folder contains a `.gitkeep` file. The folders are:

- the standard folder of the domain, with `scripts/decisions/`, `logs/jobs/`, `logs/services/`, `data/markets-catalog/`, `data/polymarket-prices/`, `docs/common/`, `docs/how-to/` and `docs/index/`;
- one strategy, `strategy-1-agent/`;
- one example trading agent below the strategy, `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`. The word "momentum" is only a placeholder.

The old files of the domain are in the git history. Its docs folder `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/` contains earlier notes. They are kept for stage two. In stage two, the project writes the domain again from these files. The domain then gets its own vision, README and rebuild prompt.

**Later trading domains** are copies of the prediction-market domain, for example copy trading. The owner asks for them. At this time, none is in the tree.

Its docs: `agents/trading/prediction-market/prediction-market.index.md`. Stage two adds its `README.md`.

### What every trading domain holds

Each trading domain has the same types of trading parts in its standard folder. The prediction-market domain defines them first. A copied domain keeps their shape.

- **The trading settings of the domain** are one file in its `configs/` folder. This file contains:
  - risk limits for the full domain, for each agent and for each venue;
  - the trading accounts;
  - the venues, fees and market filters;
  - the currency;
  - the order stop switch;
  - the trade alerts that go to the owner.

  In the prediction-market domain, the file is `prediction-market-agents.config.json`. Trading agents connect to it through a file link. A trading agent can only make the limits tighter (proposal).
- **The shared trading scripts** are in `scripts/decisions/`. These scripts buy, sell and check risk. Their names are `[name].decision.[ext]`. The trading domains add the script type `decision` to the system types `worker` and `system`. Each order goes through a decision script. The decision script reads the mode and the limits before it does an action. Trading agents link the scripts that they need.
- **The order logs** are in `logs/services/[service]/`. The service that places an order logs it. This is true for test orders and live orders.
- **The docs of the domain** are in `docs/`. In the prediction-market domain, this folder contains earlier notes. They are kept for stage two.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of each trading domain

### Names of strategies and trading agents

The name of a trading agent starts with its strategy. The name ends with its AI model and its mode. The format is `[strategy-id].[own-name]-v[N].[platform-model]-[test|live]`. An example is `pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test`. The folder of a trading agent has the same name as the agent.

The ID of a strategy agent also contains its main model and its mode, for example `pm-strategy-1-agent.opus55-test`. The folder of the strategy keeps a simple name, for example `strategy-1-agent/`.

Names use only lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `.`. The maximum length is 64 characters. The owner decided that the name starts with the strategy. The exact format is a proposal.

A changed setting, instruction or script makes a new trading agent. Then `v[N]` increases by one. A different model changes the model part of the name. Do not change or use again a name. A test version and a live version are different agents.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of the prediction-market domain, in stage two

### Accounts, keys and real money

A trading account is an account or a wallet at a venue. A trading agent can use it. The trading settings of the domain list the accounts. Each account entry has these data:

- its ID and its venue;
- its mode;
- funded or not funded;
- approved by the owner or not approved;
- the agent that uses it;
- its maximum capital;
- the names of its keys.

Keys follow the key rules of the Agent OS. The key values are only in the `.env` files in `.secrets/test/` and `.secrets/live/`. Git does not keep these files. All other files use only the key names. Each key name has a prefix for its account, for example `POLYMARKET_ACCT1_API_KEY`. The system script `load-secret` gives the keys of an account to one process at a time. It refuses live keys if the owner did not approve the account.

Only the owner can:

- approve an account with real money;
- add its live keys;
- change the risk limits or the accounts.

An agent cannot approve an account. This is true for itself and for other agents.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of the prediction-market domain, in stage two

### Test and live

Each trading agent starts in test mode. This is also true for each version that self-improvement makes. In test mode, the system simulates each order at the price at the time of the decision. On blockchains, test mode can also use a test network.

A trading agent goes live only when the owner approves it. The owner must also give it a funded and approved account. A new strategy configuration starts only after the owner reads a report on it and approves it.

At this time, agents place orders only on blockchains. They can use all networks and apps. Centralised exchanges and other apps are only sources of information.

Each decision script checks two stop switches before each order: the general stop switch of the system and the order stop switch of the domain. It does this in test mode and in live mode. The two stop switches are proposals. The effect of the order stop switch on open positions is an open question.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of the prediction-market domain, in stage two

### Metrics and comparing versions

The system measures trading agents on money. It also uses the cost, speed and error measures of the system. We propose these measures:

- realised profit and loss, unrealised profit and loss, and the return on capital, from the order logs;
- win rate, with the number of trades;
- the largest fall from a peak and the current fall from a peak;
- calibration: the forecasts of the agent compared with the results and with the market price;
- AI cost for each trade.

The system compares the versions of one strategy over the same period and the same capital. It compares test results with test results. The measures that decide success are an open question.

Its docs: the `docs/README.md` file of the prediction-market domain, in stage two

### Making a new trading domain

A new trading domain is a copy of the prediction-market domain. The owner asks for it. Do these steps:

1. Use the system script `create-agent` to make the domain agent and its folders. Do not copy the folders by hand.
2. Keep the levels, the standard folders, the shape of the trading settings and the decision scripts.
3. Change the parts of the new domain: venues, fees, market filters, information sources, strategies and risk limits.
4. Start the domain with no funded account.

If two domains need the same trading part, move that part up into `agents/trading/`. Until then, keep it in the domain.

Its docs: `agents/trading/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`

### The trading dashboard

`apps/trading-ui/` is the planned dashboard of the prediction-market domain. On this page, the owner sees each trading agent and its results. The owner approves real money there, and stops or deletes agents. The folder stays in `apps/`. It is empty at this time. It is an open question if the project needs it.

Its docs: `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md`

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Trading's folder | `agents/trading/trading.index.md` | a short description of the folder |
| Trading's docs | `agents/trading/docs/docs.index.md` | the purpose of each doc |
| Research studies | `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md` | the studies and how agents use them |
| Prediction-market domain | `agents/trading/prediction-market/prediction-market.index.md` | its folders at this time. Its vision, README and rebuild prompt come in stage two |
| Trading dashboard | `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md` | the planned dashboard |
| The system above | `agents/system/docs/README.md` | all the parts that all agents share |

## Still open in the design

- **Trading folder:** Which parts go up into `agents/trading/` when there are two trading domains?
- **Domains:** Which trading domain is next, and when? Copy trading is the probable next domain.
- **Names:** Is `v[N]` part of the trading agent or part of the strategy? Do strategy folders also contain the model and the mode? Do folders use the shorter form `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/`?
- **Safety:** What does the order stop switch do with open positions? What are the capital limits of the first live accounts? How do account entries connect to key prefixes?
- **Metrics:** Which measures decide success? Where does the system keep positions? Where does the system record market results?
- **Self-improvement:** Can a strategy put a winning change into itself without the owner? Can it stop losing versions without the owner?
- **Owner:** Which channel sends trade alerts to the owner?

# Trading in the Agent OS: vision (outline)

## In short
One paragraph: what trading is in the Agent OS, how a trading domain works, the first domain, how a new one starts, and where trading stands.

## Why trading has its own place
Why everything about money lives in one place, the many ways to make money, and the goals for trading.

## The concept
Trading as a folder of domains, not an agent; what it holds; the three levels of a trading domain; the standard folder; what stays in a domain until it is shared.

## How trading should work
The loop in numbered steps, from an idea to a strategy, its versions, the owner's approval, test runs, comparison, self-improvement and real money.

## What every trading domain shares
The money rules every trading domain follows, each as a plain statement, with our proposals marked.

## How a new trading domain is made
A copy of the prediction-market domain: what it keeps, what it changes, how it starts.

## Examples
Two worked examples from start to end, using only decided rules.

## What the owner sees and does
A short list of how the owner steers trading.

## Where it stands and what comes next
What exists today, stage one and stage two, the first run and later domains.

## Principles
The rules of thumb, each with its reason.

## Ideas we are still weighing
Each idea as problem, idea and what it would change.

## Open questions
What only the owner can answer, each with why it matters.

## Going deeper
The README's path.

nodes.questions_md:
# Questions: vision.md

## Open questions for the owner

- **Which numbers decide the success of a trading agent?** The candidates are profit and loss, win rate, the largest fall from a peak, calibration and cost. The answer sets the target of self-improvement. It also sets when a version wins.
- **What are the capital limits for the first live accounts?** They set the maximum cost of a mistake when real money starts.
- **What does the order stop switch do with open positions?** To close positions, the system must send orders, but the switch refuses new orders. The vision cannot give the stop rule before this is decided.
- **Can a strategy add a winning change to itself, or retire losing versions, without the owner?** The answer decides how fast the strategies improve. It also decides how much the owner must examine.
- **Which trading domain comes next, and when?** An earlier input named copy trading as the next domain. The vision shows it only as an example until the owner asks for it.
- **Which names do the trading agents and the strategies have on disk?** The current names are `strategy-1-agent/pm-strategy-1.momentum-v1.opus55-test/`. The stage-one request used `strategy-1/strategy-1.v1.Claude-Opus5.5/`. The vision uses the current form until the owner decides.
- **Through which channel does the owner get the trade alerts?** The vision tells that alerts exist. It does not tell how they come.
- **Do the order executor and the single ledger become part of the design?** Today they are ideas that we examine.

## The owner's questions

None recorded yet.

# [agent-name]/

## What it is

The name pattern for one folder link per strategy, named after the strategy's folder (for example `strategy-1-agent/`) and pointing at that strategy's `docs/`. Through it the domain would read the strategy's docs without copies, and its variants' docs one `subagents.link/` further down. Relink, a planned shared script, is meant to build and remove it; it is read-only and never listed in a links file.

## Who looks after it

It is written by relink (stage two script).

## When and how it changes

In stage two, relink makes a real link when a strategy is created and removes it when the strategy is stopped. It is a name pattern, not a real item: it tells what each item made from it will hold.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the prediction-market domain agent (stage two).

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md` and its folder's How it works file `agents/trading/prediction-market/docs/subagents.link/subagents.link.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It links to `agents/trading/prediction-market/strategy-1-agent/docs/`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Where the project is now: stage one"), `agents/trading/docs/README.md` (section "The trading domains") and `agents/system/docs/rebuild-prompt.md` (section "Child links").

## Keep in mind

- When you need a strategy's files changed, leave it to the strategy; the domain writes only its own files.

nodes.how_md:
# prediction-market-research/

## What it is

Forty-two studies of ways to make money on prediction markets, numbered `01` to `34` and `50` to `57`, one Markdown file each, such as market making, arbitrage across venues, trading on news and sports feeds, forecasting models and copy trading; some describe practices to avoid. `_evidence/` holds the background evidence (`E1` to `E9`) with the strategy lists, and `_pipeline/` the scripts and notes that produced the studies. The first Polymarket strategy is meant to be chosen from here.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the Polymarket strategy survey sessions (2026-09-20 to 2026-09-29) and `agents/trading/researches/prediction-market-research/_pipeline/stage2-write-verify.js`.

## When and how it changes

It changes when a survey session writes the next batch of studies (58 to 84 are briefed but not written) or runs stage 3 (overview, ranking, conclusions).

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner; knowledge-base-agent (when it writes the trading docs); and the prediction-market domain agent, when it chooses the first strategy (stage two).

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `agents/trading/docs/README.md`, `agents/trading/researches/prediction-market-research/_pipeline/HANDOFF.md` and its folder's How it works file `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It is built from `agents/trading/researches/prediction-market-research/_evidence/`. It is written by `agents/trading/researches/prediction-market-research/_pipeline/`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md`, `agents/trading/docs/README.md` (section "Research studies") and `agents/trading/researches/researches.index.md` (section "Keep in mind").

## Keep in mind

# apps/

## What it is

Applications and projects: our own apps, the outside apps we use and repositories cloned only to study them. Today it holds `docs/` (the apps vision, README, README twin and rebuild prompt), the owner's project IDE in `project-IDE/` (the File Tree page, its server and this project's records), the prediction-market domain's trading dashboard in `trading-ui/`, empty and waiting for stage two, and `temp/` for research clones. Every app has its own `docs/`. An outside app we use is meant to be forked on GitHub and get its own folder with `docs/` and `repo/`: `main` holds our changes, `upstream` follows the source. None is brought in yet. Still open: whether agents may clone on their own and how a fork sits in the repository.

## Who looks after it

It is written by the owner, knowledge-base-agent and project-ide-agent (ide-sync).

## When and how it changes

It changes when an app is added, updated from its source or removed, or the rules for outside code change.

## Who uses it, and when

It is read by the owner, every agent before working on an app and an AI rebuilding the repository.

## Where it is mentioned

It is described in `apps/docs/README.md`, `apps/docs/vision.md`, `docs/README.md` and its folder's How it works file `agent-os.index.md`.

## Related knowledge

It is built from `apps/docs/rebuild-prompt.md`. The rules that apply to it come from `agents/system/CLAUDE.md` (section "Rules"), `docs/metadata.md`, `apps/docs/README.md` and `docs/README.md` (section "Apps").

## Keep in mind

- When you clone a repository only to study it, put it in `temp/`; never commit the clone.
- When we start using an outside app, fork it first and change only our `main` branch; never change `upstream`.
- When an app is added, updated from its source or removed, update its docs and its row in the apps list in the same change.

# README.md

## What it is

The full and exact description of the `apps/` folder: every app with its kind, place and state, how the folder is laid out, each part (the apps docs, the project IDE, the prediction-market dashboard, research clones, apps we use from outside), the list of apps, and where each app's own docs are.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent, with the `readme-doc` skill and its outline for an app. The owner can also change it on the File Tree page.

## When and how it changes

After every change to an app or to the rules for outside code, after the vision and before the ASD-STE100 version and the rebuild prompt. The agent rewrites the parts the change touches, checks every "Its docs" path is real, and updates the list of apps and the open points.

## Who uses it, and when

Readers after the vision, the owner after a round of changes, and every agent before it works on an app it does not know. It is where an AI finds which app lives where and where its docs are.

## Where it is mentioned

The apps vision's last section; its ASD-STE100 twin `README.asd.md`, which follows it section by section; the apps rebuild prompt; the system README's part on apps and the IDE.

## Related knowledge

The vision gives the why; the rebuild prompt gives the exact build; each app's own README goes deeper. For now it also holds the list of apps as a table, a proposal until the owner says where the list lives.

## Keep in mind

- When you change it, rewrite `README.asd.md` to match in the same change.
- When an app is added, updated from its source or removed, update its row in the list of apps.
- When you name a path, make sure it exists.

# Questions: README.md

## Open questions for the owner

- **Where do we keep the list of apps?** The planned separate list file is not used now, and it is empty. For now, we propose the table in this README. The answer decides where the row of each app is.

- **Does `apps/trading-ui/` get its own `docs/` now, or when its design starts in stage two?** Each app must have a `docs/` folder. Today it has only its How it works and Details files.

# Apps (ASD-STE100)

This file is the ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English version of `apps/docs/README.md`. `README.md` is the source. If the two files do not agree, `README.md` is correct.

## In short

Apps are programs that help people and agents to use the Agent OS. There are three kinds of app: our own apps, forks of outside apps that we use, and research clones of outside code. Each app has its own vision, README and rebuild prompt. Now, `apps/` has one app that operates: the project IDE of the owner. The dashboard of the prediction-market domain is an empty folder. No outside code is in the project now.

This document gives a full description of the `apps/` folder. It gives each app, the layout of the folder, the rules for outside code and the location of the docs of each app. The vision tells why the system has apps. The vision is at `apps/docs/vision.md`.

## The apps at a glance

| App | Kind | Function | Location | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Project IDE | ours | It shows the project to the owner: the File Tree page, its server and the knowledge of the project | `apps/project-IDE/` | It is complete and the owner uses it |
| Prediction-market dashboard | ours | It shows the trading agents of that domain and controls them | `apps/trading-ui/` | Empty folder; stage two; possibly not necessary |
| Research clones | research clone | Copies of outside repositories, only for study | `apps/temp/<name>/` | None now |
| Apps we use | fork | Outside programs that the project uses, kept as our fork | `apps/<name>/` | None now |

The connections between the apps and the system:

1. The owner uses the page of the project IDE.
2. The page writes the changes of the owner into the files of the repository.
3. On the server, the page sends each request to Claude Code. Claude Code starts in `agents/system/`.
4. The project IDE agent and its skills build the page again from the files.
5. Each AI reads the same files before it makes a change.
6. A research clone goes into `apps/temp/<name>/repo/`. After the study, the clone is deleted. The results go into the research folder of the agent that did the study.
7. An app that we use is a fork on GitHub. The fork goes into `apps/<name>/repo/`. The branch `main` is ours. The branch `upstream` follows the source.

## How the folder is laid out

```
apps/
├── apps.index.md            How it works of the apps folder
├── apps.meta.json           Details of the apps folder
├── docs/                    the docs for all apps (this folder)
│   ├── vision.md            why the system has apps; the function of each kind
│   ├── README.md            each app and the path to its docs
│   ├── README.asd.md        this file
│   └── rebuild-prompt.md    the instructions for an AI to build apps/ again
├── project-IDE/             the IDE of the owner (our app)
│   ├── docs/                its vision, README, README.asd.md and rebuild prompt
│   ├── current-ui/          the File Tree page and its data, published on claude.ai
│   ├── server/              the same page on the server of the owner, with Claude Code
│   └── data/                the knowledge of the project and the records for the page
├── temp/                    research clones: <name>/repo/ is not committed; <name>/docs/ only on request
└── trading-ui/              the dashboard of the prediction-market domain: empty now
```

An outside app that we use gets its own folder at this level: `apps/<name>/`. This folder has `docs/` and `repo/`. No such folder is in the project now. The tree shows no example.

Each file and each folder of our own apps has a How it works file (`x.index.md`) and a Details file (`x.meta.json`). Each folder of `apps/` also has these two files. The four docs in `apps/docs/` also have an Example file (`x.example.md`) and a Questions file (`x.questions.md`). An outside app is different. Its three docs are its only metadata now. The files in its `repo/` folder get no metadata.

## The parts

### The apps docs

`apps/docs/` describes the apps folder as one unit. It has this README, the vision, the rebuild prompt and `README.asd.md`. `README.asd.md` has the same content as the README in Simplified Technical English. Thus, you can compare the two files.

The facts come from the notes of the system in `apps/project-IDE/data/`. The facts also come from the docs of each app. The knowledge base agent writes these docs. The agent uses the skills `vision-doc`, `readme-doc` and `rebuild-prompt-doc`, in that sequence. The agent writes them again when an app is added, changed or removed. The details of an app stay in the docs of that app. This folder gives only a summary.

Its docs: `apps/docs/docs.index.md`

### The project IDE

`apps/project-IDE/` is the IDE of the owner. It is our most important app. The owner builds the Agent OS with plain words, and AI writes the plans, docs and code. The IDE helps the owner to understand the result.

The IDE shows the project as a tree. Each file and each folder has tabs: the file, How it works, Details, and Example and Questions when these files exist. Some kinds of file have more tabs. The owner can edit, comment, ask questions and delete items. The button Apply changes moves all changes into the files. Each AI uses the same tree. The tree tells the function of a file, the files that depend on it and the files that must change with it.

The IDE has four folders:

- `current-ui/` has the page `file-tree-explorer.html`, its data `file-tree.data.json` and `real-files.json`, the text of each file. The build makes the two data files. Do not edit them manually. The page is published on claude.ai.
- `server/` has `server.py`, `claude_bridge.py`, `voice.py`, `server.config.json` and `README.md`. These files operate the same page on the server of the owner. On the server, notes and edits go directly into the files. A request on the page operates as a Claude Code session. The session starts in `agents/system/`. The service accepts connections only from the same machine. The owner connects through an SSH tunnel. Push, delete, install, live actions and access to `.secrets/` need the approval of the owner, or the server refuses them.
- `data/` has the records of the project: `inputs/` (each input of the owner, word for word), `decisions.md`, `changelog.md`, `plans/`, `archive/`, `overrides.json` and, on the server, `page-store/`.
- `docs/` has the docs of the IDE: `vision.md`, `README.md` (the full documentation of the IDE), `README.asd.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`.

The logic of the IDE is not in its folder. The project IDE agent and its skills `ide-build` and `ide-sync` are in `agents/system/.claude/`. The build scripts are in the skill `ide-build`. Claude Code starts in `agents/system/`, thus it loads this agent and these skills. The IDE reads all the repository. It gives the page, writes the edits of the owner into files, and keeps a record of each request.

Stage one is to complete the IDE. Do these tasks: examine each file and each folder, write custom views for the different kinds of file, and make each How it works file and each Details file correct. We propose a folder `apps/project-IDE/views/` for the shared views. This folder does not exist now.

Its docs: `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md`

### The prediction-market dashboard

`apps/trading-ui/` is for the dashboard of the prediction-market domain. The dashboard is a Next.js API and web app. With it, the owner can monitor the trading agents of that domain: their parts, logs, performance, data, decisions and the improvements in test. The owner can also create an agent from a plain description, approve a new strategy version or a live account, stop or delete agents, and ask questions to agents. Each action with live money needs the approval of the owner.

The folder is empty. It has only its How it works file and its Details file. It is part of stage two, with all the prediction-market domain. Possibly the project IDE does this function, and the dashboard is not necessary. The dashboard has no `docs/` folder now. The docs come when the design of the dashboard starts.

These questions are open: Does the dashboard read the files of the domain directly or through an API layer? How does the owner get access to it: only on the machine, or with a sign-in?

Its docs: `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md`

### Research clones

`apps/temp/` has repositories from GitHub that we copy only for study. Each repository gets a folder `apps/temp/<name>/`. The clone goes into `repo/`. Our `vision.md`, `README.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md` go into `docs/` only when the owner asks for them.

Do not commit the clone. `.gitignore` must ignore `apps/temp/*/repo/`. The agent that does the research writes the results in its own research folder. When the research is complete, delete the clone. If we decide to use the program, we make a fork. The fork goes into its own folder, not into `temp/`. Now, there are no clones. The folder has only its How it works file and its Details file.

Its docs: `apps/temp/temp.index.md`

### Apps we use from outside

We make a fork on GitHub of each outside program that the project uses. The fork goes into `apps/<name>/`:

- `docs/` has our `vision.md`, `README.md` and `rebuild-prompt.md`. The vision tells why we use this app and what we changed. The README gives the source, our fork, its branches, the commit in use, its parts, how to start and test it, and how to update it. The rebuild prompt tells how to make the fork again, the start commit and each change that we made. Now, these three docs are the only metadata of the app.
- `repo/` has our fork. We propose to keep it as a git submodule. Then the repository records the exact commit in use.

The fork has two branches. The branch `main` is ours. All our changes go into `main`, and we operate `main`. The branch `upstream` follows the main branch of the source. We do not change `upstream`.

To update the app, do these steps:

1. Get the changes from the source.
2. Move `upstream` to the new source commit.
3. Merge `upstream` into `main`.
4. Do the tests of the app.
5. Record the new commit in the docs of the app and in the list of apps.

Later, the owner can ask for a skill that changes an app fully to the system format. The proposed name of the skill is `adopt-app`. The skill gives a How it works file and a Details file to each file of the app, one job to each file, its features and the other docs. This skill does not exist now.

Now, there is no app of this kind. Possibly the first is the old Polymarket tools. This question is open.

Its docs: `apps/<name>/docs/README.md` of each app, when it exists

### The list of apps

Each app has one row in the list of apps. The row gives the name, the kind (`ours`, `fork` or `research`), the source, our fork and its branches, the commit in use, the last update from the source, and the users. Now, the list has no file. We propose that this table is the list until the owner decides its location.

| App | Kind | Source | Fork and branches | Commit in use | Last update from source | Users |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project-IDE` | ours | this repository | none | the commit of this repository | not applicable | the owner, each AI that works on the project |
| `trading-ui` | ours | this repository | none | none (empty) | not applicable | the prediction-market domain, later |

Its docs: this file

## What apps take from and give to the system

- **Apps take** the files of the repository. The project IDE reads each file, each How it works file, each Details file and the knowledge in `apps/project-IDE/data/`. A research clone gives results to the agent that does the study. Later, agents can use an outside app as a tool.
- **Apps give** the owner a method to see and control the project. They give each AI the context for a correct change. They write the edits and requests of the owner into the files.
- **Apps obey** the rules of the system. An app does not keep or show the value of a key. An app uses only key names. The values stay in `.secrets/` on the machine. No action is live without the approval of the owner. Each change starts with a plan from the skill `change-plan`.

## Where each part's docs are

| Part | Its docs | Content |
|---|---|---|
| The apps folder | `apps/docs/vision.md`, `apps/docs/README.md`, `apps/docs/rebuild-prompt.md` | why apps exist, each app, how to build the folder |
| The project IDE | `apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md` | the page, the server and the data, and how to build them again |
| The server of the IDE | `apps/project-IDE/server/README.md` | the server requirements, how to start it and connect to it, each setting |
| The knowledge of the IDE | `apps/project-IDE/data/README.md` | how the system keeps the knowledge: layers, tags, the flow |
| The build of the IDE | `agents/system/.claude/skills/ide-build/scripts/README.md` | how the build makes and checks the page |
| The dashboard | `apps/trading-ui/trading-ui.index.md` | its function and the open questions |
| Research clones | `apps/temp/temp.index.md` | the rules for a clone |
| An app we use | `apps/<name>/docs/README.md` | its source, fork, branches, commit and changes |

## Still open in the design

- **Forks:** Is `repo/` a submodule (proposed) or a clone that git ignores? Where are the forks on GitHub (proposed: the account of the owner)? How frequently do we update from the source (now: only on request; a scheduled check is an idea)?
- **Research clones:** Can agents make a clone without a request from the owner?
- **First outside app:** Do the old Polymarket tools come in as a fork?
- **The list of apps:** Where is the list: in this README (proposed now) or in a separate file?
- **The dashboard:** Is it necessary? If yes, does it use files or an API layer, and how does the owner get access? When does it get its `docs/` folder?
- **Shared views:** the proposed folder `apps/project-IDE/views/` and its file `views.json`.

Who the agent is, what it builds (only `apps/`), what it assumes exists above, what it never does.

The three kinds of app and the docs every app has, in about 150 words.

Safety, formats, metadata next to every item, the outside app exception, git.

The complete tree of `apps/` as one code block, with placeholders marked.

Folder names, the How it works and Details formats with node ids, fork branches, the list of apps row.

1. The apps folder  2. The apps docs  3. Research clones  4. The dashboard  5. The project IDE (its own prompt)  6. Apps we use; each with the files to create and its check.

Numbered steps, each with its check; where each app's own prompt is followed.

## Acceptance checks
Runnable checks that prove `apps/` is the same.

## Do not build
Open points and ideas, with what to leave in their place.

# Questions: vision.md

## Open questions for the owner

- **Can agents clone an outside repository for research without you, or only when you ask?** The answer sets how freely agents can learn from the code of other persons.
- **Are the earlier Polymarket tools our first app, as a fork?** The answer decides the first outside app. It also decides the tools of the prediction-market domain.

how.text: The page itself: the tree of every folder and file with search and filters. The tree is exactly the files git keeps and the folders that hold them, plus the two local-only `.env` files, and each item's id is its path, so the address of the page opens that item; nothing only planned is shown, a file with nothing written yet is marked "empty", and every build checks that the page tree equals the files in git, so a pulled repository and the rebuilt page show the same tree. For each item it shows its tabs: How it works, File, Example, Questions, extra tabs such as jobs, links, tests or key names, and Details. Every file shows its two metadata files as rows right under it, its How it works (`vision.index.md` for `vision.md`) and its Details (`vision.meta.json`, empty for now), and every folder shows its own first inside it; clicking one opens that tab, and the metadata switch above the tree hides or shows them. Folders start closed below the top levels; a first click on a closed folder opens it, and the search opens the folders on the way to each match. Every file and folder except the top has a Delete button next to its name: it opens a short form with an optional note for Claude, and the deletion runs the agent, which removes the item and cleans the project of it. A deleted item stays in the tree, struck through, until the next sync, and can be brought back. For now the page shows one status, "changed": a tag on whatever a request from the page touched (an edit, a note, an added or deleted item, a request in the box, a file Claude Code changed), listed on the Changed tab until the next sync. Its own File tab shows this source, the same file that is published, so the finished page is put in place before the data is built. It works in three places. On claude.ai it saves the owner's edits, notes, deletions and questions at once in its own store, and they reach the files at the next sync. An Apply changes button at the top, with the number of changed items, starts that sync: it sends Claude one comment on the page, and when Claude has applied the changes and published the new tree, the open page shows it. If no Claude is watching the page, the request is kept and the owner is asked to say "sync the file tree" in the project chat. On the owner's server it finds the server's service next to it, saves into the repository, writes edits straight into their files and sends requests, deletions and Apply changes to Claude Code. Served anywhere else it is view only and says so in its header. On the owner's server, the request box and the delete note box have a microphone button: it records up to 5 minutes, the server turns the recording into text, and the text is added to the box to check and send; on claude.ai the button is hidden.
keep: The page shows only the "changed" status for now; new statuses come only when the owner asks for them.

# Questions: file-tree-explorer.html

## Open questions for the owner

None open.

## The owner's questions

### 2026-10-01: Why were the new agent and skill not in the tree?

> why i don't see them in mine file tree

At that time, the page showed a planned tree. The build made that tree from the tree notes. The tree notes had the old agent name and no vision skill.

Today the tree is exactly the files on disk. Thus `agents/system/.claude/agents/knowledge-base-agent.md` and `agents/system/.claude/skills/vision-doc/SKILL.md` show as all other files do. The File tab shows their real text.

Docs improved: apps/project-IDE/current-ui/file-tree-explorer.index.md.

### 2026-10-05: Why are the .index.md files not in the tree?

> i still can't see .index.md files in a the tree files, why?

At that time, the page showed them only in the How it works tab, not as rows.

Today the "metadata" switch is on by default. It shows the How it works file and the Details file of each file as rows immediately below that file. The metadata files of a folder show first, in that folder. When you click one of these rows, the page opens that tab.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the metadata switch).

### 2026-10-06: Why do files show in a search but not in the tree?

> when i do search file tree i can see vision.md and another vision skill, why i don't see them in a file tree without search

They are in the tree, in folders that are closed at the start. A search opens each folder on the path to a match.

Now the first click on a closed folder opens it and selects it. The second click, or a click on its arrow, closes it.

This changed later: `vision.md` moved from `agents/system/.claude/docs/` to `agents/system/docs/`.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/current-ui/file-tree-explorer.index.md.

### 2026-10-09: Why is vision/ not in the tree?

> why i can't see it in a file tree how i said we always should have real represention of file tree on a disk and on ui

At first, the page did not show the planning folder `vision/`. This was intentional.

Now the page shows each file that git keeps, `vision/` also. It shows the two `.env` files as local-only, without their text. The build checks that the page tree is equal to the files in git.

This changed later: on 2026-10-14 `vision/` was removed from the repository. Thus the page does not show it.

Docs improved: apps/project-IDE/current-ui/file-tree-explorer.index.md.

### 2026-10-09: Why do real metadata files stay when the metadata switch is off?

> why files like .claude.meta.json not hidden when checkbox metadata off

At first, the switch controlled only the metadata rows that the page added for each item. The real metadata files on disk showed as usual files.

Now each metadata file obeys the switch. When the switch is on, each metadata file shows one time.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the metadata switch).

### 2026-10-12: Why is the tree after a pull different from the page?

> fuck man why i just pull last version and i don't have same file tree as i have on current ide

The page also showed approximately 400 planned items that were not on disk yet.

Today the page tree is exactly the files in git, plus the two local-only `.env` files. Each build checks this. Thus, after the next page build, a pulled repository and the page show the same tree.

# The project IDE (outline)

## In short
What the IDE is, in the vision's words; where it stands (stage one); what this manual covers; the vision's path.

## The IDE at a glance
One picture of the loop (repository, build, page in three places, sync) and one table: each part, what it is for, where it lives while we plan and in the finished layout. Then how the parts connect, step by step.

## How it is laid out
The finished `apps/project-IDE/` tree, one line per entry; where the agent, skills and scripts live; that every file is edited where it is.

## The page
The manual of the page, one subsection each: the header, the tree, the sheet of an item, the tabs, reading and editing a document, notes, the ask box, adding, deleting and bringing back, the "changed" mark and Apply changes, on a phone, what the browser remembers.

## The three places the page runs
A table: claude.ai, the owner's server, anywhere else; how the page knows, where work is saved, who answers, what Apply changes does. The published link and capabilities.

## What the page reads
The data file's top level and each item's fields, and `real-files.json`.

## How the page is built and checked
The `ide-build` scripts in a table, the build steps in order (including the tree-equals-git check), the rules.

## How the owner's work comes back
The store's three collections in a table, the `ide-sync` steps, the rules.

## The metadata files and the tabs
A table of the metadata files and their tabs, the naming rules, what exists today, the rule that a tab shows only when its file exists.

## The server
What it needs, how to start and reach it safely, what each file does, the settings table, the planning paths and the final ones.

## Who looks after it
The project IDE agent, the knowledge base agent, the owner.

## Tests and checks
What must pass before a publish and after a sync.

## Where each part's docs are
A table: part, its docs path, what they add.

## Still open in the design
Stage one work, then the other open details, one line each.

# README.md

## What it is

The full manual of the project IDE. It describes every part of the File Tree page and how to use it, the three places the page runs (claude.ai, the owner's server, view only), how the page is built and checked, how the owner's work comes back into the files, the metadata files behind the tabs, how to run the server, who looks after it, where every part lives now and later, and what is still open.

## Who looks after it

The knowledge base agent writes it with the `readme-doc` skill. The owner asked for it to be the complete manual of the IDE, so it is longer than the skill's usual length for an app. The owner can also change it on the page.

## When and how it changes

It changes after every change to a part of the IDE: the page, the build scripts, the sync, the server or its settings, the metadata files, or where a part lives. It is updated after the vision and before its ASD-STE100 version and the rebuild prompt. The agent rewrites the parts the change touches, keeps "Still open in the design" current and checks every docs path.

# Questions: README.md

## Open questions for the owner

- **Do we keep this README as one long manual, or move the page manual into its own file?** The skill sets 500 to 2,000 words for the README of an app. You asked for the full documentation of the IDE, thus this README has approximately 6,800 words. The answer decides where readers look for how to use the page.
- **Do the shared views go in `apps/project-IDE/views/`, with a `views.json` list?** We propose this. The answer decides where each custom view goes in stage one.

## The owner's questions

### 2026-09-29: Where do I select the model and the effort?

> i still not see where i can choose effort and better use only last one in a drop down, fable, opus 5.5 sonet 5.5 haiku

The page on claude.ai cannot select a named model or an effort level. It can only ask for one of three levels: Most capable, Balanced or Fastest. The platform then selects the model. This selection is next to the ask box.

On the owner's server, the page has no model selection. The setting `claude.model` in `server.config.json` selects the model. When it is empty, Claude Code uses its default.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the ask box and the server settings).

### 2026-09-30: How does "changed" work, and when does a sync occur?

> and how changed works, since the last sync and when and how we do sync?

The "changed" mark is on each item that a request from the page touched. Such a request is an edit, a note, an added or deleted item, or a waiting request. The Changed tab lists these items until the next sync.

A sync occurs when the owner pushes Apply changes at the top of the page, or says "sync the file tree". Then these steps occur:

1. `ide-sync` writes all changes into the files. It records each message as an owner input.
2. `ide-build` builds the page again and publishes it.
3. The marks are removed.

On the owner's server, the page writes file edits and How it works edits into the files at once.

This changed later: the first Changed view had the labels NEW, EDITED, REMOVED and COMMENTS. It became the one "changed" mark. The Apply changes button came after.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the "changed" mark and Apply changes).

### 2026-10-05: Does a file edit update the claude.ai page?

> and we now can edit this and after it ll update artefact that i can open it here or how it's works?

The claude.ai link shows the last published version. It changes only when the page is published again to the same link. That publish keeps the waiting notes of the owner.

The `ide-build` skill publishes the page at the end of each round. How the claude.ai page gets the work done on the server is still open.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the three places the page runs, and "Still open in the design").

### 2026-10-13: Can I edit a block as it shows?

> can we when we edit file block in ide  not change format to md again for editing, just same box but just edit there

Yes. Do these steps:

1. In the Read view, double-click the block. On a phone, tap it two times. The block becomes editable where it is, and it looks the same as when you read it.
2. Push Save or Ctrl+Enter, or click outside the block. The page changes the block back into Markdown and writes only those lines.

A Markdown button opens the source lines. The front matter always opens as source.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (reading and editing a document).

### 2026-10-13: What decides if a file is planned or not planned?

> what logic we currently have around planed not planed files

Today nothing decides this. The page and the build know only the files on disk. Nothing comes from a plan, and the "planned" switch is removed.

A file that has no text yet has the mark "empty". The "empty" filter shows only these files.

This changed later: at the time of the question, planned items came from the tree notes, and found items came from the disk. On the same day, the owner had all logic about planned items removed.

Docs improved: none, the answer was already in apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md (the empty filter) and agents/system/CLAUDE.md (the rules).

### 2026-10-14: Terminal or page?

> what is a differnce if exist when we ll run agent from terminal claude code and when we make notes on ui?

It is the same Claude Code, with the same `CLAUDE.md`, skills and files.

In the terminal:

1. Claude Code records the input and does the round as `CLAUDE.md` tells.
2. You name the item yourself.
3. It asks you in the terminal before risky steps.

On the page:

1. Each note is tied to one item.
2. The page saves it word for word at once, with a history and undo.
3. The item has the mark "changed" until the sync.
4. On the server, the request box runs the same Claude Code, with Allow and Refuse.

Use the page for one item. Use the terminal for work on many items. Terminal work shows on the page only after the next page build.

Docs improved: apps/project-IDE/docs/README.md, apps/project-IDE/docs/README.asd.md.
